metadata.title: AWM-Fuse: Multi-Modality Image Fusion for Adverse Weather via Global and Local Text Perception

details.application_detail: Multi-modality image fusion (specifically infrared and visible) designed to handle adverse weather conditions such as rain, haze, and snow by leveraging textual semantic information.
details.proposed_model_detail: AWM-Fuse is a unified framework that incorporates global and local text perception. It uses a Global Text Perception Module (GTPM) with BLIP-generated captions for overall scene context and a Local Text Perception Module (LTPM) with ChatGPT-generated detailed descriptions for fine-grained degradation effects. The architecture utilizes Residual State Space Blocks (RSSB) based on Mamba for efficient long-range dependency modeling and a decoder with Wavelet Convolution (WTConv) to enlarge the receptive field. A novel VLM-driven loss using CLIP aligns the fused output with clean textual descriptions.
details.dataset_description: The model is evaluated on AWMM-100k (a benchmark for adverse weather containing 2100 training pairs and 50 test images per weather type: rain, haze, snow) and standard datasets for ideal conditions including M3FD, MSRS, and LLVIP.

metadata.title: Spatial-Frequency Enhanced Mamba for Multi-Modal Image Fusion

details.application_detail: The model is designed for Multi-Modal Image Fusion (MMIF), specifically targeting Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF) to integrate complementary information for enhanced visual representation and downstream tasks like object detection and medical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: SFMFusion is a framework that utilizes a three-branch structure to couple MMIF with Image Reconstruction (IR) as an auxiliary task. It introduces the Spatial-Frequency Enhanced Mamba Block (SFMB), which consists of a Mixed-scale Mamba Block (MMB) for spatial perception, a Channel Enhanced Block (CEB) for inter-channel modeling, and a Frequency Enhanced Block (FEB) using FFT for frequency domain perception. Additionally, it employs a Dynamic Fusion Mamba Block (DFMB) to adaptively integrate features from the different branches.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on six datasets: MSRS (1,083 training pairs, 361 testing pairs), M3FD (300 testing pairs), and FMB (280 testing pairs) for IVIF. For MIF, the Harvard Medical dataset was used, including MRI-CT (21 pairs), MRI-PET (42 pairs), and MRI-SPECT (73 pairs). No fine-tuning was applied to M3FD, FMB, and Harvard Medical datasets to test generalization.

metadata.title: SDCM: Simulated Densifying and Compensatory Modeling Fusion for Radar-Vision 3-D Object Detection in Internet of Vehicles

details.application_detail: 3-D object detection for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) using 4-D radar and vision fusion to handle sparse radar point clouds and vision data degradation in low-light or occluded environments.
details.proposed_model_detail: The SDCM framework consists of three main components: the Simulated Densifying (SimDen) module, which uses 3-D Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and Gaussian simulation to generate dense radar point clouds; the Radar Compensatory Mapping (RCM) module, which leverages radar features to compensate for visual representation degradation; and the Mamba Modeling Interactive Fusion (MMIF) module, which employs a Mamba-based mechanism to reduce modality heterogeneity and achieve effective interactive fusion.
details.dataset_description: The model is evaluated on three datasets: View-of-Delft (VoD), which includes 64-layer LiDAR, 3+1-D radar, and stereo camera data; TJ4DRadSet, a dataset for autonomous driving with continuous sequences and 3-D annotations; and Astyx HiRes 2019, a small dataset containing LiDAR, radar, and camera data from urban and outskirt environments.

metadata.title: Interactive Spatial-Frequency Fusion Mamba for Multi-Modal Image Fusion

details.application_detail: The model is primarily designed for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF), with additional validation on downstream tasks like object detection and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Interactive Spatial-Frequency Fusion Mamba (ISFM) framework utilizes a Modality-Specific Extractor (MSE) based on the Vision State-Space Module (VSSM) to capture long-range dependencies. It incorporates a Multi-scale Frequency Fusion (MFF) module using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to integrate low and high-frequency components. The core innovation is the Interactive Spatial-Frequency Fusion (ISF) module, which uses frequency features to guide spatial feature fusion through Frequency-Guided Mamba (FGM) and Frequency-Guided Gate (FGG) mechanisms.
details.dataset_description: The study uses the MSRS dataset (1083 training, 361 testing pairs), FMB (280 testing pairs), and RoadScene (221 testing pairs) for IVIF. For MIF, it utilizes the Harvard Medical dataset, selecting 150 pairs for testing across MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT modalities.

metadata.title: CAWM-Mamba: A Unified Model for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion and Compound Adverse Weather Restoration

details.application_detail: The model is primarily designed for autonomous driving and UAV monitoring applications where sensors must operate under compound adverse weather conditions such as simultaneous rain, haze, and snow.
details.proposed_model_detail: CAWM-Mamba is an end-to-end framework that jointly performs image fusion and compound weather restoration using unified shared weights. It consists of three key modules: (1) Weather-Aware Preprocess Module (WAPM) for feature enhancement and global weather embedding extraction; (2) Cross-modal Feature Interaction Module (CFIM) for cross-modal alignment and feature exchange; and (3) Wavelet Space State Block (WSSB) which uses wavelet-domain decomposition to decouple multi-frequency degradations. WSSB includes Freq-SSM to model anisotropic high-frequency degradation and a Common Degradation Space Mechanism (CDSM) for unified degradation representation.
details.dataset_description: AWMM-100K contains 100,000 real and synthetic image pairs for benchmarking fusion under severe weather. For experiments, subsets were used: 700 images per single-weather type (rain, haze, snow) for training and 50 for testing; 1,000 images per compound-weather type (rain&haze, rain&snow, haze&snow) for training and 50 for testing. Standard clean datasets used for verification include LLVIP (low-light), MSRS (multi-spectral), and M3FD (multi-modal).

metadata.title: A hybrid fusion approach combining salience perception and generative adversarial networks for multimodal medical image integration

details.application_detail: The method is designed for clinical medical image fusion to enhance disease diagnosis (e.g., identifying tumors and clots) by reducing orientation errors in multimodal image integration.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Hybrid Fusion Method (HFM) combines Salience Perception (SP) with a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). SP is used to identify and prioritize unbiased grayscale features based on pixel distribution, while the GAN concurrently operates on biased and unbiased features to identify the most relevant features for maximum orientation detection and precision. The model uses a generator and discriminator to fine-tune the fusion process and minimize orientation-related errors.
details.dataset_description: The study utilized two primary datasets: 1) Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) fundus images from Kaggle, containing 3662 training and 180 testing images at 224x224 resolution across 5 disease categories. 2) Brain tumor CT images from Kaggle, consisting of 2500 training and 318 testing images, with 30 slices per patient obtained from 82 patients.

metadata.title: A multi-modal deep clustering method for day-ahead solar irradiance forecasting using ground-based cloud imagery and time series data

details.application_detail: The method is designed for day-ahead global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting to support photovoltaic (PV) power generation and energy system management.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed MMDC-MMIF framework consists of two main components: Multi-modal Deep Clustering (MMDC) and Multi-modal Irradiance Forecasting (MMIF). MMDC utilizes an encoder-decoder structure with VGG for cloud imagery and CLSTM for time series data to categorize weather patterns into clusters. MMIF then employs Swin Transformer for image feature extraction and CLSTM for time series (processed with Variational Mode Decomposition) to train specialized forecasting models for each cluster, enhancing accuracy and robustness across varying weather conditions.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes the publicly available CA dataset from a solar plant in the United States (38.64 N, 121.15 W). The dataset includes ground-based cloud imagery (downscaled to 64x64 pixels), observed GHI, and NWP GHI from the North American Mesoscale Forecast System (NAM). The data spans from March 2014 to December 2016 with a 1-hour temporal resolution. The split includes approximately 80% for training, 10% for validation, and 10% for testing.

metadata.title: A multi-scale expert gating network with cross-modal attention for multimodal medical image fusion
datasets: Chinese Abdominal Multimodal Medical Image Dataset

details.application_detail: The 'others' application domain includes fusion of Green Fluorescent Protein (GFP) and Phase Contrast (PC) microscopic images for biological research (protein localization and cellular morphology), and multi-exposure image fusion tasks from the Multi-Exposure Fusion Benchmark (MEFB) dataset, covering diverse scenarios like natural landscapes and indoor scenes under varying exposure conditions.
details.proposed_model_detail: CENet is a multi-scale expert-gating network with a cross-modal convolutional attention module. It first extracts rich multi-scale features using a multi-scale convolutional feature extractor, which includes a Dilated Convolution Feature Extraction (DCFE) module with parallel standard and dilated convolutions (dilation rates 1 and 2). A Cross-modal Feature Attention (CFA) mechanism then enhances and aligns modality-specific features by generating attention maps through grouped convolution. Unlike traditional MoE, CENet uses a compact set of four lightweight experts (CNNs with 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, and 7x7 convolutional kernel sizes) and adaptively selects expert combinations via a gating mechanism, ensuring full utilization of all experts. The network employs two serially connected expert-gating networks. The overall framework operates in a closed-loop optimization, orchestrating dynamic interactions among feature extraction, cross-modal enhancement, and fusion stages. It converts RGB functional images to YCbCr for channel matching with grayscale MRI.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard dataset is used for MRI-SPECT and MRI-PET fusion tasks, with 333 and 245 image pairs for training, respectively, and 50 image pairs for testing. A publicly available benchmark dataset of 150 paired GFP and PC microscopic images is used for generalization. The MSRS (Multi-Spectral Red-Visible Image Fusion Dataset) contains 1200 paired IR-VIS image samples (640x480 pixels) for low-light scenarios. A Chinese abdominal multimodal medical image dataset provides 250 pairs of CT-PET images. The Multi-Exposure Fusion Benchmark (MEFB) dataset is used for multi-exposure image fusion tasks.

metadata.title: A multi-view and multi-granularity emotional semantic interaction framework combining graph and attention mechanism for multimodal sentiment analysis

details.application_detail: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to distinguish emotional leanings within data by examining information across multiple modalities. It strengthens machine understanding, enhances the quality of human-machine interactions, and fuels the continuous development of wearable smart devices, digital home appliances, and intelligent sensing and control systems.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed MMIF (Multi-view and Multi-granularity Sentiment Semantic Interaction Framework) tackles challenges in multimodal sentiment analysis in four steps: (1) Quantum-inspired Temporal Feature Extraction (QTFE) enriches each modality's temporal dynamics with a quantum-structured LSTM. (2) Graph Neural Networks Enhanced Intra-modal Representation (GEIR) builds modality-specific graphs and taps diverse GNN variants (GCN for visual, GAT for text/audio) to strengthen intra-modal reasoning. (3) Inter-modal Deep Interaction Fusion (IDIF) fuses cross-modal cues using a bidirectionally enhanced attention mechanism, including a quantum-inspired cross-modal Transformer. (4) Emotion Representation Distribution Matching (ERDM) refines final emotion predictions by capturing multi-granularity distributions of sentiment intensity information, disentangling multimodal sequences into highly emotion-relevant and weakly emotion-relevant components. The framework integrates quantum computing techniques (Quantum LSTM, Quantum-enhanced Transformer) to enhance model learning capacity and capture complex temporal patterns and deep correlations.
details.dataset_description: CMU-MOSI: A corpus focused on sentiment and subjectivity analysis in online videos. It comprises 2199 short video clips extracted from 93 movie review videos, with sentiment annotations on a scale of [-3, 3]. The dataset includes 1080 positive, 1022 negative, and 97 neutral sentiment segments. Train: 1284, Valid: 229, Test: 686. CMU-MOSEI: An extension of CMU-MOSI, the largest video-level English dataset for MSA tasks, consisting of 22,856 utterance videos from over 1000 different speakers, covering 250 topics. Sentiments are annotated on a scale of [-3, 3]. As a multi-label dataset, each sample may be associated with multiple emotions, with varying levels of intensity for each emotion. Train: 16,326, Valid: 1871, Test: 4659. CH-SIMS: A multimodal sentiment analysis dataset specifically designed for the Chinese context, featuring rich character backgrounds. It comprises 2281 video clips collected from 60 scenes across various movies, TV shows, and variety programs. Each video clip is annotated once for multimodal sentiment and three times for uni-modal sentiment, with sentiment intensity rated on a scale of [-1, 1]. Train: 1368, Valid: 456, Test: 457.

metadata.title: A nested self-supervised learning framework for 3-D semantic segmentation-driven multi-modal medical image fusion

details.proposed_model_detail: The Nested Self-supervised Learning Framework (NSLF) is a novel approach for 3-D semantic segmentation-driven multi-modal medical image fusion. Its architecture comprises four main components: a Contrastive U-Net (CU-Net) for feature extraction, a Fusion Convolutional Decoder (FCD) for image fusion, a Geometric Matching Network (GMN) for semantic alignment, and a Feature Segmentation Decoder (FSD) for segmentation. CU-Net extracts multi-scale features from single-mode images using contrastive learning. FCD reconstructs the fused image. GMN ensures spatial semantic consistency between fused and source images through geometric spatial consistency learning. FSD predicts segmentation results from source image features. The framework utilizes a nested self-supervised training strategy, where components are fine-tuned sequentially across three stages: feature extraction, multi-modal fusion, and semantic segmentation, leveraging cooperative learning of fusion and segmentation tasks.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge 2021 (BraTS 2021) dataset. This dataset includes multi-contrast MRIs, specifically T1-weighted (T1), T1-weighted with contrast enhancement (T1ce), T2-weighted (T2), and Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) modalities. Each MRI is accompanied by a ground truth label with four classes: background, edema, non-enhancing tumor core, and enhancing tumor core. The training set consists of 126 multi-contrast MRIs with identical modalities and ground truths, while the validation set comprises 126 multi-contrast MRIs with varying degrees of segmentation complexity.

metadata.title: A two-stage multimodal learning framework based on text-driven vision pretraining and cross-modal feature fusion for thyroid ultrasound diagnosis

details.application_detail: Thyroid nodule ultrasound diagnosis using multimodal data integration.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Two-stage Text-driven Multimodal Network (TTM-Net) utilizes a two-stage training paradigm. In the first stage, Text-Driven Vision Pretraining (TDVP) aligns visual features from a CNN encoder with textual features from a frozen BERT encoder using large-scale unlabeled text-image pairs. In the second stage, visual and textual features are integrated via the Cross-Modal Concat-Attention Fusion (CMCAF) module for supervised classification. The model is optimized using a hybrid loss function combining cross-entropy and feature alignment losses.
details.dataset_description: Dataset 1 (Primary) contains 22,544 thyroid ultrasound images from 9466 patients, including 12,174 pathologically confirmed images evenly split between benign and malignant cases. Dataset 2 (External) consists of 7653 images from 2294 patients used for generalizability testing. Both datasets include Structured Descriptions (key-feature listings) and Detailed Descriptions (full-sentence reports) based on the proposed TNUFCS-AI schema.

metadata.title: AFDFusion: An adaptive frequency decoupling fusion network for multi-modality image

details.application_detail: The paper addresses multi-modality image fusion (MMIF), specifically infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) and medical image fusion (MIF), aiming to create a single image that integrates complementary information like thermal radiation and texture details.
details.proposed_model_detail: AFDFusion is an adaptive frequency decoupling network that perceives associative invariant and intrinsic specific features among cross-modalities. It uses an Adaptive Frequency Decoupling (AFD) module to dynamically adjust low-frequency weights of the kernel. The architecture consists of a MixEncoder and MixDecoder (using ResBlocks and Lite Transformer blocks). It follows a two-stage training strategy: Stage I involves contrastive self-supervised decoupling and reconstruction, while Stage II incorporates Invariant Fusion Layers (IFL) and Specific Fusion Layers (SFL) to produce the final fused image.
details.dataset_description: Training is conducted on the MSRS dataset (1083 pairs). Testing for IVIF is done on TNO (40 pairs), M3FD (300 pairs), and FLIR (40 pairs). Medical image fusion is tested on MRI-PET, MRI-SPECT-Tc, and MRI-SPECT-Ti datasets (10 pairs each) from the Harvard Medical website. The VIFB benchmark (21 pairs) is also used for evaluation.

metadata.title: All-weather multi-modality image fusion: Unified framework and 100k benchmark

details.application_detail: The paper addresses the challenge of infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) under adverse weather conditions like rain, haze, and snow, where visibility is reduced and modality information becomes imbalanced.
details.proposed_model_detail: AWFusion is an end-to-end unified framework that integrates deweathering and fusion. It consists of a fusion module and a restoration module. The fusion module uses Learned Low-Rank Representation (LLRR) to decompose images into low-rank components (fused via Sparse Transformer Blocks) and sparse components (fused via a Sparse Feature Prediction Block). The restoration module employs a U-Net backbone augmented with STBs and a Physical-Aware Clear Feature Prediction Block (PFB) guided by the Atmospheric Scattering Model to predict light transmission and restore clear features. It utilizes distillation learning from multiple teacher networks specialized in different weather types to handle diverse degradations.
details.dataset_description: The authors construct AWMM-100k, a large-scale benchmark containing 100,000 registered multi-modality image pairs. It covers three major weather degradations (rain, haze, and snow) with three degradation levels (light, medium, and heavy). The dataset includes both synthetic scenes generated via a phenomenological pipeline and real-world scenes collected using a DJI M30T drone, featuring diverse environments such as urban, suburban, rural, and natural settings, and includes object detection labels.

metadata.title: Analytical and experimental investigation of vibration response for the cracked fluid-filled thin cylindrical shell under transport condition

details.application_detail: The study focuses on the vibration response and state identification of fluid-filled thin cylindrical shells (FTCS) with surface cracks, which are essential components in pipelines, marine installations, and aerospace vehicles.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method integrates the FlÃ¼gge shell model, Linear Spring Model (LSM), and linear potential flow theory to solve the free vibration response of cracked FTCS. It also introduces a natural frequency isoline-based state recognition method to identify crack morphology and fluid state by finding unique intersection points of frequency isolines.
details.dataset_description: The research uses literature data from reference [49] for preliminary verification, FEM simulation data for numerical validation, and experimental data from a multi-channel LMS vibration test platform using four 20# steel shells with relative crack depths of 0, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7.

metadata.title: APGFusion : Adaptive PoolFormer and CNN medical image fusion network based on convolutional gated linear units

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on multimodal medical image fusion, specifically combining structural (CT, MRI) and functional (PET, SPECT) images to provide comprehensive diagnostic information for clinical analysis.
details.proposed_model_detail: APGFusion is an adaptive dual-branch network that balances global and local features. It utilizes a shared encoder containing TransGLU modules (based on TransNeXt) to extract shared features. The architecture splits into a base PoolFormer extraction branch for global structural features and a detail CNN extraction branch (using Inverted Residual Blocks) for local details. A novel Adaptive Feature Fusion (AFF) module in the decoder dynamically adjusts feature weights across modalities using channel and spatial attention mechanisms to ensure visual naturalness and structural integrity.
details.dataset_description: The model was trained and tested on the Harvard Medical Dataset, which includes 810 pairs for training (CT-MRI, PET-MRI, SPECT-MRI) and 137 pairs for testing. Additionally, 21 pairs of T1-T2 images from the BraTS dataset were used for testing. Training samples were preprocessed into 128x128 blocks.

metadata.title: ATDFusion: Adapter-Tuned Dual-Branch Network for multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MRI-CT, MRI-PET, MRI-SPECT) designed to assist in clinical diagnosis by combining anatomical and functional imaging information while balancing global semantic consistency and local detail preservation.
details.proposed_model_detail: ATDFusion is an asymmetric dual-branch network consisting of a Primary Semantic Branch (Transformer-based) and a Detail Compensation Branch (CNN-based). The semantic branch utilizes a frozen DINOv2 backbone with a Low-Rank Dynamic Token Adapter (LR-DTA) that adaptively adjusts fine-tuning parameters (token count and rank) based on input complexity. The detail branch uses a frozen VGG16 to capture high-frequency textures. A Fusion Enhancement Guidance (FEG) module integrates multi-scale features under the supervision of a saliency-aware loss to preserve diagnostically critical regions.
details.dataset_description: The study uses the Harvard Medical School dataset, partitioned into MRI-CT (334 train/42 test), MRI-PET (309 train/20 test), and MRI-SPECT (486 train/47 test) pairs, all pre-registered at 256x256 resolution. Additionally, the HECKTOR 2025 dataset (160 slice pairs) is used for zero-shot generalization and downstream tumor segmentation tasks.

metadata.title: CAWM-Mamba: A unified model for infrared-visible image fusion and compound adverse weather restoration

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Multimodal Image Fusion (MMIF) under adverse weather conditions, including single degradations (haze, rain, snow) and compound degradations (e.g., haze&rain, rain&snow). The application domains include autonomous driving, UAV monitoring, military reconnaissance, medical diagnosis, and environmental monitoring. The goal is to generate clearer, more informative fused images with higher information density, better visual perception, and stronger environmental adaptability, thereby enhancing target detection, scene understanding, and decision-making capabilities.
details.proposed_model_detail: CAWM-Mamba is an innovative end-to-end framework designed for jointly performing infrared-visible image fusion and compound adverse weather restoration with unified shared weights. The architecture comprises three main components:1. Weather-Aware Preprocess Module (WAPM): This module preprocesses input weather-interfered visible light images, enhances degraded visible features, and extracts global weather embeddings. It uses two convolutional layers and ReLU activation functions for initial feature extraction, global average pooling to compress the feature map into a global feature vector, and channel attention (Sigmoid function) for channel-wise weighting. This generates a fixed-dimensional global feature embedding (Fembedding) that provides explicit prior guidance for subsequent tasks.2. Cross-modal Feature Interaction Module (CFIM): This module facilitates the alignment of heterogeneous modalities (infrared and visible) and the exchange of complementary features. It performs feature extraction and dimension unification via 1x1 convolution. Features are divided into two parts: one for salient features/thermal contours (MaxPooling) and another for texture/scene details (AvgPooling). Attention weights are generated using convolutional networks (Conv7, Softmax) and applied to features, followed by dimension concatenation.3. Wavelet Space State Block (WSSB): This novel technique addresses complex weather changes by transforming degradation-containing images into the wavelet domain using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). It decouples multi-frequency degradations into low-frequency (ILL) and high-frequency (IHL, ILH, IHH) components. Within WSSB, there are two sub-modules:Freq-SSM: This module models anisotropic high-frequency degradation without redundancy. It performs bidirectional scanning in three directions for high-frequency components, applies LayerNorm, and uses a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to capture long-range dependencies, aligning the scanning trajectory with the dominant direction of each subband.Common Degradation Space Mechanism (CDSM): This lightweight mechanism learns a unified degradation representation to improve robustness against varying composite degradations. It is implemented as a simple residual block with convolution and channel attention, enabling the network to capture shared patterns across multiple weather types.
details.dataset_description: The AWMM-100K dataset was primarily used for experiments, containing 100,000 real and synthetic image pairs for evaluating fusion capabilities under severe weather conditions. For single-degradation scenarios, 700 images per weather type (rain, haze, snow) were used for training, and 50 distinct images per type for testing, ensuring no scene overlap. For compound-degradation scenarios, 1000 images per type (rain&haze, rain&snow, haze&snow) were used for training, and 50 distinct images for testing, separate from the single-degradation sets. Additionally, LLVIP, MSRS, and M3FD datasets were used to evaluate the model's performance in ideal, clean multi-modal image fusion scenarios. These datasets represent generic scenarios with different scene contexts and mild noise distributions.

metadata.title: CLTE: Infrared and visible image fusion through cross-domain learning and texture-contrast enhancement

details.application_detail: The paper addresses challenges in accurately and continuously monitoring animal activities in intensive livestock farming environments. Single-modal imaging is limited by low-light conditions, noise, blur, motion interference, and texture degradation. Image fusion of infrared and visible modalities is proposed to highlight thermal targets while preserving fine visual textures, providing comprehensive scene representation for tasks like pig identification, segmentation, and temperature measurement.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed CLTE (Cross-domain Learning and Texture-contrast Enhancement) framework is designed for infrared and visible image fusion in intensive livestock farming. It comprises three main modules: 1) Feature Extraction: Uses multiple convolutional layers for shallow features (local semantic information) and four Swin Transformer layers for depth features (global semantic information). 2) Cross-domain Fusion: Employs a synergistic attention-based module with a shifted window mechanism for self-attention (intra-domain fusion) and Multi-head Cross Attention (MCA) for inter-domain interactions, enabling efficient interaction between local and global representations. 3) Texture-contrast Enhancement: Utilizes multi-scale convolution operations and a contrast block to adaptively emphasize texture and contrast cues, enhancing visual clarity and detail perception even under low illumination. This module calculates a contrast map based on standard deviation and applies transformations to generate an activation vector for contrast weights, which are then multiplied with mainstream features. A feature reconstruction module (Transformer and CNN-based) maps the fused deep features back to the image space.
details.dataset_description: A new benchmark dataset, the 'intensive pig farming dataset', was collected at the Jinshui Pig Breeding Farm in Hubei Province from July to December 2022, between 6:00 AM and 7:00 PM. Data was recorded hourly. The pig pens measured 4m x 4m x 1m. The MAG64AI smart thermal imager was used for simultaneous collection of infrared (640x480) and visible (1440x1080) images. The camera was positioned 4.5m directly above the pig pens. The dataset contains 648 high-quality initial infrared-visible pairs, registered using the ReDFeat algorithm, with a resolution of 1440x1080. Additionally, the MSRS dataset (1083 training pairs, 361 testing pairs, 640x480 resolution, road scenes) and the LLVIP dataset (16,836 pairs, 1280x1024 resolution, low-light vision) were used for training and testing, respectively.

metadata.title: Clusters in chaos: A deep unsupervised learning paradigm for network anomaly detection

details.application_detail: Network anomalies pose a significant threat to information systems due to cyberattacks, system malfunctions, or configuration errors, leading to disruptions, data breaches, and financial losses. The paper addresses the urgent need for robust mechanisms to detect and mitigate these anomalies early, especially in the face of increasing complexity and frequency of cyber threats. The proposed model aims to identify unusual network activity in real-time to prevent catastrophic consequences.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed model, named Cluster Autoencoder Pair (CAEP), is a novel deep unsupervised learning paradigm for network anomaly detection. It integrates clustering and autoencoder methods. First, K-Means clustering is applied to group similar normal network traffic data points into distinct clusters. Then, individual deep autoencoders are trained for each specific cluster. This approach allows the autoencoders to learn nuanced patterns of normal behavior within each cluster. An autoencoder is a feedforward neural network consisting of an encoder and a decoder. The encoder compresses input data into a lower-dimensional latent space through two hidden layers (e.g., 32 and 16 neurons) using ReLU activation. The decoder reconstructs the original input from this compressed representation through similar hidden layers, with the final layer using a sigmoid activation function. The model is optimized using the Adam optimizer and Mean Squared Error (MSE) as the loss function. Anomaly detection is performed by establishing a threshold based on the mean and standard deviation of reconstruction errors for each cluster. Data points with reconstruction errors exceeding their cluster-specific threshold are classified as anomalous. The system leverages Euclidean distance for clustering and t-SNE and PCA for visualization.
details.dataset_description: The NSL-KDD dataset is a widely used benchmark for cybersecurity and intrusion detection, an updated version of KDD Cup 99. It consists of network traffic data from a simulated environment, labeled with different attack categories. It comprises 148,517 rows and 42 features, with 77,054 normal traffic and 71,463 anomalous traffic data. The CIC-IDS-2017 dataset is also used to assess generalization capabilities. It contains 58,712 data points.

metadata.title: CMMDL: Cross-modal multi-domain learning method for image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Multi-Modal Image Fusion (MMIF) to generate fused images that facilitate visual perception and scene understanding. It specifically addresses Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF). IVIF is crucial for tasks like object detection and semantic segmentation in complex environments, while MIF is important for combining information from different medical imaging modalities (MRI-CT, MRI-PET, MRI-SPECT) to aid diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: CMMDL (Cross-Modal Multi-Domain Learning) is a multi-domain learning method for multi-modal image fusion. It consists of four core components: 1. Multi-Domain Learning Shared Encoder (MDLSE): Uses a shared Restormer structure equipped with a Spatial-Frequency domain Cascaded Attention (SFCA) mechanism. SFCA integrates spatial and frequency domain information to capture complex precision details and comprehensive pixel-level features, avoiding inconsistencies across modalities. 2. Dual-Domain Parallel Learning Strategy: This includes the Spatial Domain Learning Block (SDLB), which employs a dual-branch structure based on Invertible Neural Networks (INN) for lossless information propagation and extracting modality-specific features in the spatial domain, and the Frequency Domain Learning Block (FDLB), which utilizes cross-modal deep perceptual Fourier transforms to capture continuous and precise global contextual information, using fused phase information for comprehensive scene representation. 3. Heterogeneous Domain Feature Fusion Block (HDFFB): Promotes feature interaction and fusion between different domains and modalities through various pixel-level attention structures to obtain the final output image. The model aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that primarily focus on the spatial domain and neglect valuable frequency domain information, which often leads to loss of high-frequency details.
details.dataset_description: MSRS (Multi-Spectral Road Scene) contains 1083 pairs of infrared and visible images for training and 361 pairs for testing. It is used for IVIF and semantic segmentation (9 object categories: background, bump, color cone, guardrail, curve, bike, person, car stop, car). TNO contains 25 pairs of infrared and visible images and is used for testing IVIF performance. LLIVP (Low-Light Visible-Infrared Paired) contains 250 pairs of infrared and visible images and is used for testing IVIF performance. M3FD (Multi-Modal Multi-task Fusion Dataset) comprises 4200 paired infrared and visible images annotated with six distinct categories (people, car, bus, motorcycle, lamp, truck) and is used for object detection. The Harvard Medical Image dataset consists of 150 image pairs selected for MIF, including 50 pairs each for MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT fusion tasks. The model trained on IVIF is directly generalized to MIF tasks without additional fine-tuning.

metadata.title: CoRFusion: Collaborative infrared-visible restoration-fusion via degradation-aware dynamic experts

details.application_detail: Multimodal image fusion is widely utilized in domains such as security surveillance and autonomous driving. Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) is among the most representative tasks. IVIF has been widely applied in fields such as pedestrian detection and recognition, video surveillance, and autonomous driving. The proposed CoRFusion method is specifically formulated to perform optimally in complex and dynamically changing outdoor environments characterized by severe physical degradations, including extreme illumination fluctuations, adverse weather (dense fog and haze), and sensor-induced degradation (thermal noise, quantization noise, optical defocus).
details.proposed_model_detail: CoRFusion is a degradation-robust paradigm for infrared and visible image fusion in degraded scenarios. It's a novel Restoration-Fusion Network built upon a coordinated framework of specialized processing experts. The network pioneers a new learning paradigm where image restoration and information fusion are inherently and jointly optimized to counteract complex degradations. It employs a degradation-aware dynamic expert mechanism, autonomously routing features to specialized restoration experts pixel by pixel. The overall architecture is a symmetric, dual-encoder U-Net paradigm comprising three core processes: feature encoding, hierarchical recovery and fusion, and feature decoding. The core is the Degradation Restoration Block (DRB), which uses an Iterative Spatial Routing Mechanism with a sequence of dedicated expert steps to progressively refine features, performing dense, pixel-level routing to adaptively handle spatially heterogeneous degradations. A synergistic loss function (Ltotal) is developed, incorporating components for fusion (Lfusion), reconstruction (Lrecon), and cross-modal recovery (Lcross). Single-modal reconstruction and cross-modal recovery tasks, introduced as self-supervised signals, promote the learning of generalizable feature representations and enhance robustness under complex degradations.
details.dataset_description: A large-scale, multi-degradation image fusion dataset was constructed using 300 perfectly aligned, high-quality, and non-degraded image pairs from FMB and MSRS datasets. It was split into 270 pairs for training and 30 pairs for testing. Seven distinct degradations (visible overexposure, underexposure, fogging, blurring, infrared optical noise, thermal noise, and quantization noise) were applied, resulting in 2400 sample pairs (2160 training, 240 testing). The degradation simulation is governed by physical characteristics of multimodal optical imaging, replicating real-world environmental constraints for visible images (overexposure, underexposure, blur, haze via generative diffusion model) and thermal sensor physics for infrared images (thermal noise, optical system degradation, quantization noise). Public datasets used for evaluation include: RoadScene (221 image pairs, focuses on traffic environments, dynamic targets like vehicles and pedestrians), M3FD (4200 pairs of diverse scene images spanning urban, rural, and motorway environments), MSRS (1444 pairs of urban road scene images covering both normal and low-light conditions), FMB (Full-time Multi-modality Benchmark) (1500 pairs of spatially and temporally registered infrared and visible images with 800x600 resolution, covering various extreme environments such as fog, heavy rain, and low light), TNO (60 pairs of military surveillance scene images, encompassing complex environments such as day-night transitions and adverse weather conditions), and LLVIP (3362 pairs of low-light images, captured nocturnally, specifically designed to evaluate algorithmic performance under extreme illumination conditions.

metadata.title: Diesel particulate matter health impacts in California: Trends, source apportionment, and policy implications

details.application_detail: The study aims to quantify ambient exposure to diesel particulate matter (DPM) and assess associated health risks (cancer and non-cancer) across California, analyze trends between 2012 and 2017, and perform source apportionment to identify the relative contributions of different emission sectors.
details.proposed_model_detail: The methodology utilizes an integrated modeling framework combining the Weather Research and Forecast (WRF) prognostic model for meteorology, the Mesoscale Model Interface Program (MMIF) for data processing, and CALPUFF (a 3D non-steady-state puff dispersion model) to simulate DPM concentrations at fine spatial resolutions (census block/tract levels). Health impacts are assessed using OEHHA guidance for cancer risk and the Environmental Benefits Mapping and Analysis Program (BenMAP-CE) for non-cancer mortality impacts.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes emission inventories from the California Emissions Projection Analysis Model (CEPAM) for off-road, area, and stationary sources, and the EMFAC2017 model for on-road sources. It also incorporates the U.S. EPA's 2017 National Emissions Inventory (NEI) for cross-border impacts from Mexico. Population data is based on the 2010 U.S. Census. Model evaluation was conducted using black carbon (BC) and elemental carbon (EC) data from the SCAQMD MATES-V study.

metadata.title: Differential out-of-distribution error guidance for unknown bearing fault diagnosis with conditional diffusion model

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, specifically addressing the challenge of identifying unknown or out-of-distribution (OOD) faults, including single and compound faults, which are not present in the training data.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed CD-DOE (Conditional Diffusion - Out-of-Distribution Error) framework consists of three main components: 1) CL2FV (Class Label to Feature Vector) transformation using a ResNet-based encoder to extract semantic features; 2) CD-DSR (Condition-Guided Diffusion Model for Differential Sample Reconstruction) which uses a DDPM guided by feature and temporal embeddings to reconstruct signals; and 3) a weighted OOD scoring mechanism. The model is designed to accurately reconstruct in-distribution (ID) samples while intentionally amplifying reconstruction errors for OOD samples to facilitate their detection.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes two datasets: 1) The PU (Paderborn University) dataset, which includes normal and real bearing damage samples from accelerated life testing with a sampling frequency of 64 kHz. 2) The DB dataset, a custom-built test bench dataset simulating various fault conditions (ball, inner ring, outer ring, composite, and gear faults) with a sampling frequency of 12.8 kHz. Both datasets are split into ID and OOD categories for experimental validation.

metadata.title: DIFusion: Multimodal medical image fusion based on detail preservation and invertible neural networks

details.application_detail: The model is designed for multimodal medical image fusion, specifically integrating structural information from MRI and CT with functional data from PET and SPECT. It also extends to infrared and visible image fusion for general scenarios like road surveillance.
details.proposed_model_detail: DIFusion is an invertible neural network-based framework that decomposes source images into high-frequency detail components (HFDC) and low-frequency base components (LFBC) using a DCT-based method. The HFDC is enhanced via a Multi-Scale Invertible Enhancement Module (MS-IEM) consisting of a Scale Feature Extraction Block (SFEB) and a Conditional Reversible Network (CRN). The CRN utilizes the bidirectional invertibility of INNs to prevent information loss. The LFBC is optimized through a Base Layer Enhancement (BE) module with multi-branch structures. Finally, the components are reconstructed into a fused image.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard Medical Dataset is used for medical image fusion, containing 800 training pairs (294 MRI-CT, 209 MRI-PET, 297 MRI-SPECT) and 30 test pairs for each modality. The MSRS (Multi-Spectral Road Scenarios) dataset is used for infrared-visible fusion, containing 1083 training pairs and 361 test pairs.

metadata.title: DMCMFuse: A dual-phase model via multi-dimensional cross-scanning state space model for multi-modality medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-modality medical image fusion (MMIF) designed to combine complementary information from different imaging modalities (e.g., CT for bone structure and MRI for soft tissue) to enhance diagnostic accuracy and clinical analysis.
details.proposed_model_detail: DMCMFuse is a dual-phase framework. The first phase utilizes a Hierarchical Attention Enhancement-based Feature Decomposition (HAED) module to decompose source images into coarse structure and fine texture layers while ensuring spatial and channel consistency. The second phase employs a Multi-dimensional Cross-scanning Fusion Mamba (MCFM) module, which integrates spatial scanning, spatial interaction, and channel scanning. This module leverages the Mamba architecture to establish strong cross-modal correlations and capture both global and local features for high-quality image reconstruction.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated using 1202 aligned multi-modality medical image pairs from the Harvard Medical website. The dataset includes four fusion tasks: 228 MRI-CT pairs, 106 MR/T1-MR/T2 pairs, 329 MRI-PET pairs, and 539 MRI-SPECT pairs. All images have a resolution of 256x256 pixels. The training set was expanded to 30,000 pairs through data augmentation (rotation, cropping), and 120 pairs were used for testing.

metadata.title: DMF-LP: Enhancing image quality through multimodal medical image fusion using diffusion and Laplacian techniques

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MIF) designed to integrate complementary information from different sensors (e.g., MRI, CT, PET) to enhance image quality for precise lesion localization and quantitative diagnosis in clinical scenarios like cancer diagnostics.
details.proposed_model_detail: DMF-LP is a multimodal medical image fusion framework that integrates Laplacian pyramid decomposition with diffusion models. It features a pre-fusion module (LP-F) that uses Laplacian pyramids to extract and retain texture and edge information before the forward diffusion stage. The model employs a pixel-by-pixel fusion strategy where source images and the pre-fused image participate in forward diffusion with shared noise. In the reverse process, a U-Net denoising network iteratively removes noise to generate the final fused image. The training process is optimized using a hybrid multi-objective loss function grounded in information entropy theory, incorporating global, local, and time-step entropy terms to maximize information retention and ensure stable convergence.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated using two datasets: 1) The publicly available Harvard Medical dataset, from which 184 pairs of CT and MRI images were extracted for training to ensure robustness across brain pathologies. 2) A proprietary dataset consisting of 800 image pairs from colorectal cancer patients, where each pair contains a plain CT image (providing anatomical structure) and an enhanced CT image (providing lesion details via contrast agents), used for testing and validation.

metadata.title: DMFusion: A dual-branch multi-scale feature fusion network for medical multi-modal image fusion
datasets: Chinese Abdominal Multimodal Medical Image Dataset

details.application_detail: High-quality multi-modal image fusion is crucial for improving diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging. It integrates information from different modalities like CT (dense structures), MRI (soft tissue details), PET (metabolic/functional info), and SPECT (blood flow) to provide comprehensive and accurate images for diagnosis, treatment planning, and surgical navigation. Specific applications include MRI-CT for radiation therapy planning, MRI-PET for tumor localization, MRI-SPECT for cerebrovascular diseases, and PET-CT for surgical planning in cancer patients.
details.proposed_model_detail: DMFusion is a dual-branch autoencoder (AE) network designed for medical multi-modal image fusion. One branch extracts modality-specific distinctive features, while the other captures shared features between modalities. The encoder employs multi-scale feature extraction techniques, enhancing perception of image details across various scales. Both encoder and decoder use lightweight self-attention mechanisms, specifically Restormer blocks for shallow feature extraction and CMT blocks (modified with ConvNeXt blocks for Local Perception Unit replacement) for deep feature extraction. The model uses designed selection rules to precisely select salient features from the two branches, which are then fed into the decoder for deep fusion and reconstruction. It operates with a two-stage training approach: an initial reconstruction stage to learn inherent modality characteristics, followed by a fusion stage.
details.dataset_description: The study uses two main datasets. The Harvard Medical dataset comprises 540 pairs of medical images, including 50 MRI-CT, 205 MRI-PET, and 285 MRI-SPECT images. The second dataset is an abdominal multi-modal medical image dataset from China, consisting of 250 pairs of CT-PET images. Both datasets are fully anonymized, contain no identifiable patient information, and adhere to strict ethical standards for research involving sensitive medical data. Five-fold cross-validation was performed on both datasets.

metadata.title: Domain-guided mixture of experts for EEG-based emotion recognition

details.application_detail: The application domain is EEG-based emotion recognition (EER), specifically addressing the challenge of inter-individual variability in EEG signals, often referred to as domain shift. The goal is to achieve accurate predictions on data from unseen subjects, which is paramount for developing robust, real-world brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. The paper focuses on domain generalization (DG) to subjects that are entirely unseen during training.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Domain-Guided Mixture of Experts (DGMOE) is proposed to enhance the generalization capability of the MoE framework for cross-subject EER. It leverages the expert specialization mechanism of the MoE for specialized regional processing and introduces a domain-guided two-level screening mechanism. The model architecture consists of multiple stacked layers, with each layer integrating four pivotal modules: multihead attention for temporal feature extraction, a domain-guided dynamic router for channel-level domain-sensitive routing, a mixture of graph experts for spatial feature processing, and domain-guided expert screening for region-level domain-sensitive feature selection. The dynamic router adaptively calculates the number of allocatable experts based on channel domain sensitivity, restricting the influence of highly individualized channel inputs. The domain-guided screening module performs refined selection, aggregating only the most subject-invariant outputs generated by experts, rather than aggregating all expert outputs.
details.dataset_description: SEED: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 15 healthy individuals, each undergoing three experimental sessions. Participants viewed 15 film clips designed to elicit positive, negative, and neutral emotions. EEG signals were captured using a 62-channel ESI NeuroScan system at 1000 Hz. Precomputed DE features, extracted using a nonoverlapping 1-second window across five frequency bands, were used. Data from the first session was selected for cross-subject EER. SEED-IV: Similar to SEED, this dataset includes 15 participants across three sessions. The stimuli consisted of 24 movie clips targeting four distinct emotional states: happiness, neutrality, sadness, and fear. Data from the first session was selected for cross-subject EER. THU-EP: This dataset features EEG data from 80 subjects. Each participant watched 28 video clips to evoke a broad spectrum of emotional responses (anger, disgust, fear, sadness, amusement, joy, inspiration, tenderness, arousal, valence, familiarity, liking). Ground-truth labels were derived from participants' self-reported scores on emotional dimensions. EEG data was acquired using a 32-channel system at 250 Hz, with preprocessing for cross-subject EER.

metadata.title: Dual adaptive soft thresholding multimodal networks with contrastive augmentation for intrapartum fetal monitoring

details.application_detail: Intrapartum fetal monitoring to assess fetal health status by integrating cardiotocography (CTG) recording fetal heart rate (FHR) and uterine contraction (UC) signals, and maternal clinical data. The goal is to provide objective and accurate assessment methods to assist obstetricians in clinical interpretation, addressing limitations of existing methods such as lack of dedicated denoising for UC signals, insufficient comprehensive fusion of multimodal data, and class imbalance.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Dual Adaptive Soft Thresholding Multimodal Networks (DAST-MMNet) is a deep learning framework designed for robust intrapartum fetal monitoring. It consists of three main components: a feature extractor with the Adaptive Soft Thresholding Block (AST-Block), a multimodal fusion network with the Smooth Adaptive Threshold Attention Fusion Module (SAT-AFM), and a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) classifier. The AST-Block dynamically suppresses extrinsic noise in intrapartum UC signals and eliminates artifacts from feature fusion. The SAT-AFM, built upon a logarithmic smooth threshold function, bridges semantic gaps between modalities and adaptively recalibrates channel-wise thresholds. The feature extractor employs large-kernel convolutional layers and ResNets. A contrastive augmentation strategy with focal loss addresses class imbalance, and a re-mask mechanism prioritizes discriminative features. Grad-CAM++ is used for model interpretability.
details.dataset_description: The CTU-UHB dataset, a collaborative collection from the Czech Technical University in Prague and the University Hospital in Brno, comprises 552 meticulously selected intrapartum records. Each record contains 90-minute prenatal CTG signals, enriched with maternal basic information, detailed labor process accounts, neonatal condition evaluations, and other factors affecting fetal health. Cases are classified based on postnatal umbilical artery pH, with 447 normal cases (80.95%) and 105 abnormal cases (19.02%). Data preprocessing includes removing missing values, outlier processing, FHR signal normalization, quality assessment (excluding signals with scores below 0.6), truncation of signals to 25 minutes, and augmentation using a sliding window approach (5 min step for abnormal, 20 min for normal).

metadata.title: Enhanced multimodal medical image fusion: A hybrid SWT and saliency-guided refinement approach
compared_methods: Wavelet Packet Transform with Self-Adaptive Operator
Spectral Total Variation with Dynamic Threshold Neural P Systems
NSST with Co-occurrence Filter and Local Extrema

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MÂ³IF) improves diagnostic interpretation by combining information from different medical modalities (such as CT, MRI, PET, SPECT) into a single image. The goal is to enhance diagnostic accuracy by preserving fine details (small lesions), anatomical boundaries, texture patterns, and maintaining global intensity distribution and local details, while eliminating noise and artifacts.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed SWT-SWR is a hybrid framework combining Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT) and Saliency-guided Weighted Refinement (SWR). It operates in three stages: 1. Multiscale Decomposition: Source images (CT, MRI) are decomposed into low-frequency coefficients (LFCs) and high-frequency coefficients (HFCs) using a 3-level SWT with Daubechies-1 wavelet. 2. Component-wise Fusion: LFCs are fused using a spatial-frequency-based weighted averaging rule. HFCs are fused using local energy computation and a pixel-wise maximum energy selection rule. Inverse SWT is then applied to reconstruct a preliminary fused image (FSWT). 3. Guided Filter-Based Refinement and Saliency Fusion: The preliminary fused image is post-processed using a guided filter for edge-aware smoothing, resulting in a refined fused image (FGuided_Filter). Finally, a gradient-based saliency map (using Sobel operator) is used to adaptively blend the SWT-fused and guided filter-based refined images, emphasizing diagnostically important regions and producing the final fused image (FFinal). The method aims for shift-invariant multiscale coefficient separation, energy-adaptive detail preservation, intermediate structural stabilization, and dual-domain saliency reconciliation.
details.dataset_description: The study uses an open-source public dataset [37-39] for evaluation. Dataset 1 (CT-MRI brain/head): Consists of CT and MRI image pairs. CT images provide details on bone/skull, while MRI images provide soft-tissue contrast. Dataset 2 (CT-MRI brain/head): Also consists of CT and MRI image pairs, focusing on high-frequency preservation and contrast stability. Dataset 3 (MRI-PET brain): Consists of MRI and PET image pairs. MRI provides anatomical information, and PET provides functional and metabolic activity. All input images are resized to 256 Ã— 256 pixels for experiments.

metadata.title: Entropy-aware dynamic path selection network for multi-modality medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-modality medical image fusion (MMIF) for clinical interventions, diagnosis, and treatment effect evaluation of tumors, kidneys, spinal cord injury, vascular status, intracranial hemorrhage detection, and fracture examination. The goal is to improve the accuracy of clinical diagnosis by combining anatomical, physiological, and metabolic information from different modalities (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT) to overcome limitations of single-modality images such as low resolution, blurred texture, and noise.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Entropy-aware Dynamic Path Selection Network (EDPSN) is proposed to address the problem of uneven fusion and artifacts in edge regions by considering the varying distribution of spatial information within medical images. The model consists of three main modules: 1) Edge Enhancement Module (EEM): Mitigates artifacts in edge regions by applying a central concentration gradient (CCG) to the intensity component of the PET image (after converting it to HSI color space). 2) Entropy-aware Division (ED) module: Delineates the spatial information levels of distinct regions (low, middle, high) in the image through entropy convolution and adaptive thresholds. This module reflects the information richness across different regions. 3) Dynamic Path Selection (DPS) module: Enables adaptive fusion of diverse spatial information regions based on the divisions provided by the ED module. The network processes MRI and PET/SPECT/CT images, extracts shallow features, applies EEM to PET, then uses ED to divide regions, and DPS for adaptive fusion. Finally, the fused features are compressed by a four-convolutional layer and inversely converted to RGB images.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard Whole Brain Atlas dataset was used, containing three multi-modality image pairs: MRI-CT (205 pairs), MRI-PET (311 pairs), and MRI-SPECT (417 pairs). All images have a size of 256x256 pixels. MRI and CT images are single-channel, while PET and SPECT are three-channel images, with pixel intensity ranging from [0, 255]. The data was divided into training and test sets with a 9:1 ratio, and the training data was further split 8:2 for training and validation. Additionally, the CHAOS dataset, which contains 190 pairs of MRI-CT images of abdominal organs, was used to verify the robustness and generalization performance of the EDPSN.

metadata.title: FDFusion: Efficient text-guided infrared-visible image fusion via fine-tuned lightweight VLM and Dual-branch feature modeling

details.application_detail: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) for enhancing scene perception in complex environments, with applications in object detection and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: FDFusion is an efficient text-guided infrared-visible image fusion framework. It uses a fine-tuned lightweight Vision Language Model (SmolVLM2) to generate high-quality textual descriptions as prior information. The model features a dual-branch encoder with a Texture Encoding Branch (TEB) based on DenseNet and a Contextual Encoding Branch (CEB) based on D-RAMiT blocks. A Text-Guided Attention (TGA) module enhances visual features through cross-modal interaction. The decoder uses Restormer blocks and a Cross-Layer Modality Attention (CLMA) module for explicit alignment and selection across semantic depths.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes the VLFDataset for text-guided fusion. Training is performed on 1083 image pairs from the MSRS dataset. Evaluation is conducted on the remaining 361 MSRS pairs, as well as 100 pairs from the M3FD dataset and 70 pairs from the RoadScene dataset for generalization testing. Images are processed in grayscale, normalized to [0,1], and cropped to 288x384.

metadata.title: FDPMambaFuse: A frequency-domain and parallel Mamba-based model for multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: The model is designed for multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF), integrating complementary information from different imaging modalities like CT, MRI, PET, SPECT, and PA-US to support clinical diagnosis and analysis, such as tumor detection and localization.
details.proposed_model_detail: FDPMambaFuse is a fusion network combining frequency-domain decomposition with multi-directional parallel Mamba. It features a multi-level CNN-Mamba feature extractor where CNNs capture shallow spatial features and a DWT-based parallel Mamba module models multi-scale frequency components and long-range dependencies. It includes a dual-stage fusion module with channel interaction and spatially adaptive attention, and an unsupervised hybrid loss combining pixel-level uncertainty with image gradients.
details.dataset_description: Two main datasets are used: 1) The Harvard Brain Atlas dataset containing CT, MRI, SPECT, and PET images of various pathological conditions at 256x256 resolution. 2) The HIT-MMIF-PAUS dataset, a newly constructed high-quality photoacoustic-ultrasound fusion dataset featuring mouse tumors, human skin, and fingers, acquired using linear-array, ring-array, and endoscopic imaging systems.

metadata.title: FFSWOAFuse: Multi-modal medical image fusion via fermatean fuzzy set and whale optimization algorithm

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a multi-modal medical image fusion (MMIF) method to integrate anatomical and functional information from different medical imaging modalities like MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT to assist in clinical diagnosis and surgical planning.
details.proposed_model_detail: FFSWOAFuse is a four-stage fusion framework. First, it uses a Gaussian filter for two-scale decomposition into base and detailed layers. Second, base layers are converted to Fermatean Fuzzy Images (FFIs) using an optimized parameter from Fermatean Fuzzy Entropy (FFE) and fused via similarity and texture-based rules. Third, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) generates optimal weights for merging detailed layers based on a fitness function of cross-correlation and edge similarity. Finally, the fused image is reconstructed by combining the processed layers.
details.dataset_description: The experimental evaluation uses 71 medical image pairs from the Harvard Whole Brain Atlas and other public sources. The pairs are divided into five groups: Group-1 (10 pairs of MR-T1 and MR-T2), Group-2 (20 pairs of MRI and CT), Group-3 (1 pair of T1-MR and MRA), Group-4 (20 pairs of MRI and PET), and Group-5 (20 pairs of MR-T2 and SPECT). All images are 256x256 pixels.

metadata.title: FiTNet: Frequency information guided topological relationship enhancement network for X-ray vascular segmentation

details.application_detail: Accurate segmentation of vascular structures in X-ray angiography images, specifically targeting coronary arteries and adrenal microvessels, to assist in diagnosis and treatment planning of vascular diseases.
details.proposed_model_detail: FiTNet is a frequency information guided topological relationship enhancement network based on the UNet architecture. It features three core modules: 1) Multi-Scale Frequency Domain Guidance Module (MS-FDGM) in the encoder, which utilizes Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and multi-directional Sobel operators to capture vascular patterns and low-contrast structures. 2) Spatial-Channel Graph Convolution Module (SCGCM) in the bottleneck, which employs a dynamic, learnable adjacency matrix to model inter-channel semantic dependencies and preserve topological continuity. 3) Multi-Level Feature Aggregation Module (MLFAM) in the decoder, which uses asymmetric convolutions and attention mechanisms to bridge the semantic gap between hierarchical features.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on four datasets: DCA1 (134 X-ray coronary angiograms at 300x300 resolution), XCAD (126 annotated coronary angiograms at 512x512 resolution), CHUAC (30 coronary angiographic images upscaled to 512x512), and DP-A (a private adrenal microvascular angiography dataset with 90 annotated cases at 512x512 resolution).

metadata.title: FQCDM: Feature quantization-based cardiac image diffusion synthesis model

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on cardiac image synthesis to address challenges in cardiac image segmentation, such as limited high-quality datasets, class imbalance, and artifacts. Synthetic data is used for data augmentation, self-supervised pre-training, and combined with traditional data augmentation to improve segmentation model performance and generalization ability in cardiac segmentation tasks.
details.proposed_model_detail: FQCDM (Feature Quantization-based Cardiac Diffusion Model) is a novel algorithm for cardiac image synthesis. It integrates feature quantization into the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) to generate compressed latent features, which are then quantized to produce high-quality synthetic cardiac images. The reverse denoising process of DDPM is guided by real image labels to enhance the model's focus on semantically meaningful regions. A dual-branch discriminator (DBD) is designed, comprising PatchGAN (for global feature discrimination) and EdgeGAN (for precise edge information detection), to ensure image quality and diversity. The FQB (Feature Quantized Vector Block) includes an encoder, decoder, and a Feature Vector Quantization Block with a Transformer-based codebook. The FDGB (Feature Diffusion Generation Block) uses a 2D U-Net for reverse denoising, guided by real label maps.
details.dataset_description:
The study utilizes two publicly available datasets:
1. MMWHS-2017: This cardiac segmentation challenge dataset comprises 120 multimodal whole-heart images, including 60 cardiac CT/CTA scans and 60 3D cardiac MRI scans, encompassing the entire cardiac substructure. The training set includes 20 CT and 20 MRI images, while the test set consists of 40 CT and 40 MRI images.
2. ACDC: This dataset consists of multi-slice 2D cardiac magnetic resonance images (cine MRI) from 100 patients, covering five categories of clinical diagnoses (Normal, Dilated Cardiomyopathy, Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy, Myocardial Infarction with Heart Failure, and Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy). Each case includes a series of short-axis cardiac MRI images covering the entire cardiac cycle, with segmentation labels provided for the left ventricle (LV), right ventricle (RV), and myocardium (Myo) at two time points: end-diastole (ED) and end-systole (ES).
For both datasets, slice images were divided into training, validation, and test sets in a 7:2:1 ratio. Various data augmentation strategies, including random flipping, random rotation, distortion, random cropping, and random horizontal/vertical translation and flipping, were applied to the training set.

metadata.title: Frequency-aware and cross-mamba-enhanced medical image fusion for a real-time surgical navigation framework
datasets: Intraoperative MRI Data from Human Cadavers
Intraoperative MRI Data from Healthy Volunteers

details.application_detail: The paper addresses real-time 2D-3D medical image fusion for surgical navigation, particularly in robotic-assisted interventions. It aims to integrate complementary information from multiple modalities, such as intraoperative low-resolution 2D MRI and preoperative high-resolution 3D MRI, to generate an updated, high-resolution 3D anatomical model for accurate surgical guidance and real-time decision-making. The framework is designed to overcome challenges like incomplete feature integration, loss of high-frequency structural details, and poor real-time performance in existing fusion methods.
details.proposed_model_detail: FACMFusion is a frequency-aware and Cross-Mamba-enhanced multimodal image fusion network. The framework first employs a super-resolution network (convolutional encoder-decoder) to enhance low-resolution intraoperative MRI slices to high-resolution. Then, a slice-to-volume registration network (Siamese network with VGG16 backbone) aligns the enhanced 2D slices with preoperative 3D MRI volumes. The core FACMFusion network then fuses these aligned 2D slices using two main components: 1. Cross-Mamba Interaction Module (CMIM): This module enables efficient feature interaction by combining global spatial modeling (using State Space Model blocks) with local detail enhancement (using Multi-Layer Perceptrons) to capture long-range dependencies and refine local details. 2. Frequency-Aware Selection Module (FASM): This module preserves high-frequency anatomical structures and textural details. It uses Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to decompose input features into four sub-bands (LL, LH, HL, HH) and applies channel-wise attention to selectively fuse corresponding sub-bands from target and reference streams, allowing for content-adaptive weighting per frequency band. The network uses a patch embedding layer, encoder, decoder, shallow fusion module, and deep fusion module.
details.dataset_description: The method was validated on three types of datasets: 1. Intraoperative MRI Data from Human Cadavers: Collected during simulated needle insertion procedures. It includes preoperative 3D MRI volumes and real-time intraoperative 2D MRI slices. 2D slices are 100x100 pixels with 2x2mmÂ² in-plane resolution and 1mm thickness. 3D volumes are 320x280x240 voxels with 0.8x0.8x0.8mmÂ³ isotropic resolution, resampled to 320x256x256. It comprises 308 aligned pairs, with 24 for testing and 284 for training. 2. Intraoperative MRI Data from Healthy Volunteers: Comprises preoperative 3D MRI volumes and intraoperative 2D image sequences. 2D slices are 80x80 pixels with 2.75x2.75mmÂ² in-plane resolution and 5.5mm thickness. 3D volumes are 390x480x480 voxels with 0.47x0.47x0.47mmÂ³ isotropic resolution, down-sampled to 390x256x256. It includes 186 image pairs. 3. Harvard Whole Brain Atlas Datasets: Publicly available datasets used for three multimodal image fusion tasks: CT-MRI (184 pairs), PET-MRI (269 pairs), and SPECT-MRI (357 pairs). All images were resized to 256x256. For each task, 24 pairs were selected for testing, and the remainder for training.

metadata.title: FS-Diff: Semantic guidance and clarity-aware simultaneous multimodal image fusion and super-resolution

details.application_detail: FS-Diff addresses the challenges in multimodal image fusion (MMIF) and super-resolution, particularly in real-world applications like military reconnaissance, long-range detection, and UAV aerial photography, where source images often suffer from low resolution and weak semantic information. The method aims to integrate complementary information from diverse sensors to generate informative fused images with superior visual perception and scene/target representation. It is applied to medical image fusion (MIF) to represent metabolic and structural information, and visible and infrared image fusion (VIRF) to preserve high-spatial-resolution texture and thermal target information. The proposed AVMS dataset, with its annotated targets (cars, buses, trucks, electric vehicles, people, tents, boats), supports advanced vision tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation, crucial for autonomous driving, agricultural modernization, and defense science and technology.
details.proposed_model_detail: FS-Diff is a semantic-guided and clarity-aware joint image fusion and super-resolution method that unifies these tasks as a conditional generation problem. It leverages semantic guidance from a clarity sensing mechanism for adaptive low-resolution perception and cross-modal feature extraction. The process starts by initializing the desired fused result as pure Gaussian noise. A bidirectional feature Mamba (BFM) block is introduced to extract global features from multimodal images. A modified U-Net network then performs a random iterative denoising process, trained to denoise at multiple noise levels and produce high-resolution fusion results with cross-modal features and abundant semantic information, conditioned on source images and semantics. The inference phase iteratively refines noise removal from pure Gaussian noise. The clarity sensing (CLSE) mechanism, powered by a clarity-aware contrastive language-image pre-training (CA-CLIP) model, enables precise semantic embedding. CA-CLIP utilizes a pre-trained CLIP architecture for cross-modal alignment and high-quality feature extraction from low-resolution inputs, predicting image resolution types (clear/blur) to derive higher-quality semantic information. A cross-attention module injects deep semantics into the fusion features. The forward Markovian diffusion process gradually adds Gaussian noise to the HR fusion image, while the reverse Markovian process connects the noisy target image with the LR source image, constructing a joint representation in the latent space.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes several datasets for training and evaluation across VIRF, MIF, and multifocus tasks. For VIRF, four datasets are used: LLVIP (12025 training, 3463 test), MÂ³FD (3780 training, 300 test), MSRS (1083 training, 362 test), and the newly constructed AVMS (400 training, 200 test). The AVMS dataset comprises 600 aligned visible and infrared image pairs, 8991 annotated targets, covering diverse lighting (daytime, dusk, nighttime, complex weather) and scenes (residences, roads, campuses, parks, streets, stadiums, parking lots, croplands). Images in AVMS have resolutions of 1280x1024 and 4000x3000, which were cropped and registered. For MIF, Harvard Medical SPECT-MRI (497 training, 55 test) and Harvard Medical PET-MRI (287 training, 32 test) datasets are employed, with both modalities blurred. For multifocus image fusion, Lytro [122] and MFI [123] datasets are used. For all experiments, HR fusion images were obtained via CDD, and LR source images were generated by bicubic down-sampling from HR images. Test sets for public datasets were cropped to 16x16 and bicubically degraded.

metadata.title: FSGFuse: Feature synergy-guided multi-modality image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) to integrate complementary properties for a more comprehensive information representation. This is beneficial for high-level vision tasks such as object detection, semantic segmentation, tracking, night-time driver assistance, pedestrian detection, and border surveillance.
details.proposed_model_detail: FSGFuse is an AE-based Feature Synergy-Guided Fusion network with a two-stage training strategy. In Stage I, a double-branch encoder extracts source features from infrared and visible modalities. A feature synergism loss guides the encoder to perceive consistency and difference of cross-modal features, promoting feature decoupling and capturing discriminatory feature representations. In Stage II, a Feature Complementary Fusion (FCF) module integrates these complementary features and captures long-range contextual relationships, facilitating cross-modal interaction and enriching semantic information. The model aims to preserve texture details and acquire thermal target information while avoiding redundancy.
details.dataset_description: The FLIR dataset is divided into a train set (2750 pairs of 256x256 images) and a validation set (40 pairs of images). The TNO dataset consists of 40 pairs of military-related scene images used as a test set. The MÂ³FD dataset comprises 300 pairs of images covering different object types in various scenes, also used as a test set. The LLVIP dataset is utilized for object detection tasks and includes detection labels.

metadata.title: Fusion requires interaction: a hybrid Mamba-transformer architecture for deep interactive fusion of multi-modal images

details.application_detail: Multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) aims to integrate complementary information from multi-source images to enhance visual quality for downstream computer vision tasks, including semantic segmentation, pedestrian recognition, and object detection. The paper specifically evaluates its proposed method on Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF) tasks, covering modalities such as MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT.
details.proposed_model_detail:
HTM is a novel hybrid Transformer-Mamba architecture designed for deep interactive fusion of multi-modal images. It employs an encoder-decoder macro-architecture. The encoder consists of two modality-specific Transformer blocks for effective fundamental feature extraction via channel-wise attention, and one modality-interactive Mamba block for efficient feature interaction. The Mamba block integrates two key submodules: the Optimized VSSM (OVSSM) and the Cross-Modal Gated Feedforward Network (CMFFN).

The core of OVSSM is the Cross-Modal Local Feature Scanning Mechanism (CMLFSM), which reorganizes feature maps at the channel level to pair semantically similar channels across modalities for joint modeling. It utilizes a window-based feature extraction and a Mamba-inspired directional scanning strategy to serialize features, enabling deep cross-modal interaction with linear computational complexity. This mechanism ensures that information from one modality immediately modulates the SSMs update parameters before the token of the other modality is processed.

The CMFFN adaptively modulates modality-specific features.
