It takes feature maps from two modalities, processes them with depthwise separable convolutions (DConv), concatenates them, and applies Softmax activation to generate dynamic gating coefficients. These weights modulate the original modality-specific features via element-wise multiplication, effectively minimizing the flow of non-essential information. The model is trained using a two-stage strategy: first, optimizing learnable prompts via CLIP for macro-semantic representation distillation, and then integrating these prompts as semantic-guided loss components to steer the fusion network's optimization.
details.dataset_description: For Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF), the method is evaluated on three widely adopted datasets: TNO, RoadScene, and MSRS. For Medical Image Fusion (MIF), the Harvard dataset is used, covering three common modality combinations: MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT. In the experiments, 20, 40, and 70 image pairs are randomly selected from each category for training, with corresponding test sets comprising 20, 20, and 30 image pairs, respectively. The Harvard dataset provides diverse medical images for fusion tasks, while TNO, RoadScene, and MSRS offer various scenes for visible and infrared image fusion.

metadata.title: FusionIFHM: infrared and visible light video fusion method based on intra-frame correlation features and human visual measurement feedback

details.application_detail: The method is designed for the fusion of infrared and visible light video to integrate cross-modal features, specifically targeting military surveillance, complex lighting environments, and remote sensing. It aims to improve visual quality for human perception and enhance performance for downstream tasks such as object detection.
details.proposed_model_detail: FusionIFHM (Infrared and Visible Light Video Fusion based on Intra-frame Correlation and Human Visual Measurement) integrates four components: 1) an intra-frame correlation feature extraction model using chunked ridge regression to mine complementary information; 2) an independent detail feature extraction model; 3) a control fusion model utilizing a PID control system to adaptively adjust fusion weights; and 4) a measurement feedback model that transforms images into the Human Visual Space (HVS) using a spatial frequency-aware RTV (FARTV) model and a novel HVSQAB/F metric to guide the fusion process.
details.dataset_description: The paper uses five public datasets: 1) TNO: contains military-related image pairs and video sequences. 2) BEPMS: features a long video sequence of a soldier in a jungle. 3) INO: captures image pairs and video sequences in complex scenes. 4) MSRS: consists of aligned image pairs under varying lighting conditions. 5) WHU-OPT-SAR: includes 100 pairs of registered optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images.

metadata.title: FusionOC: Research on optimal control method for infrared and visible light image fusion

details.application_detail: Infrared and visible light image fusion to solve limitations of single-type visual sensors and boost target detection performance. It is applied in object detection, pedestrian re-identification, tracking, and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: FusionOC is a fusion model based on optimal control theory. It establishes two types of mathematical models for controlled objects and uses two PID control modes based on a BP neural network for adaptive parameter regulation. The system includes a feedback mechanism to perceive feature differences between fusion results and source images, allowing it to adaptively select regulation modes based on user requirements or task characteristics. Type I regulation enhances internal feature richness, while Type II focuses on maintaining similarity and feature retention between fused and source images.
details.dataset_description: TNO: 60 pairs of infrared and visible light images in military scenes. INO: 21 frames of infrared and visible videos in different weather backgrounds. MSRS: Urban scene images including roads and pedestrian streets. MIF: Multi-focus Atlas provided by MATLAB based on common scenes.

metadata.title: Heterogeneous shareholder participation and corporate maturity mismatch: Evidence from China

details.application_detail: The paper investigates how the participation of heterogeneous shareholders (non-state shareholders in SOEs and state shareholders in non-SOEs) affects corporate maturity mismatchâ€”the practice of using short-term debt to fund long-term investmentsâ€”within the context of China's mixed ownership reform from 2009 to 2022.
details.proposed_model_detail: The study constructs a theoretical analysis framework for two-way mixed ownership reform and employs OLS regression models with firm, year, and industry fixed effects. It measures maturity mismatch (MMIF) as the difference between cash expenditure for investment and long-term financing sources relative to total assets. The model tests the "supervision incentive" effect in SOEs (where non-state shareholders reduce agency costs) and the "resource support" effect in non-SOEs (where state shareholders alleviate financing constraints and increase long-term loans). Robustness is checked using 2SLS with instrumental variables based on industry self-exclusion means of shareholding ratios.
details.dataset_description: The research utilizes firm financial data from the CSMAR database and manually gathered ownership information from annual reports and platforms like Baidu and Tianyancha.com for the period 2009â€“2022. The sample excludes "Special Treatment" (ST and *ST) companies, financial institutions, and firms with missing accounting data. The final dataset comprises 9,211 observations for State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) and 10,541 observations for non-SOEs.

metadata.title: HRSGD: High-order recurrent medical image fusion via self-supervised generative distillation

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) to integrate complementary information from various sensors like MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT to enhance clinical diagnosis. It also extends the application to infrared and visible image fusion.
details.proposed_model_detail: HRSGD is a self-supervised generative distillation framework designed for MMIF. It employs a three-stage training process: 1) A teacher network with a Dense Multi-resolution Preservation Block (DMPB) for self-supervised training. 2) A student network utilizing an Implicit Multi-resolution Block (IMB) to capture prior knowledge and Masked Generative Distillation (MGD) to restore features from the teacher. 3) A fusion network using High-order Recurrent Cross-Attention (HRCA) to capture deep dependencies between modalities through iterative semantic interaction.
details.dataset_description: The primary dataset is a publicly available collection from Harvard University consisting of 100 pairs of multimodal brain injury images for training and 100 pairs for testing, covering 10 modality combinations (e.g., CT/MR-T1, MR-T2/PET). Additionally, the MSRS and M3FD datasets are used to evaluate the model's performance on infrared and visible image fusion tasks.

metadata.title: Hybrid ABCâ€“HBA Feature Optimization with Self-Training Using Simulated Unlabelled Data for Robust Intrusion Detection

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a robust intrusion detection system (IDS) for network security, specifically optimized to detect extremely rare attack classes (U2R, R2L) under conditions of severe class imbalance.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed framework is a hybrid approach that combines swarm intelligence-based feature optimization with a self-training mechanism. It utilizes the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm for global exploration and the Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA) for local exploitation to select a compact and discriminative feature subset. A Random Forest (RF) classifier is then trained using a pseudo-labeling strategy on simulated unlabeled data to improve the model's ability to generalize to unseen or novel attack patterns.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on three datasets: 1) KDD Cup 1999, using a 10% subset for training which includes five main classes (Normal, DoS, Probe, U2R, R2L). 2) NSL-KDD, used as an external validation set to test the model's adaptability to more balanced and less redundant data. 3) CIC-IDS 2017, a modern dataset with realistic traffic scenarios, where attack categories were mapped to the standard KDD classes for consistent comparative analysis.

metadata.title: Imaging coupled filtering: A unified multi-channel framework for multimodal medical image registration and fusion
datasets: Chinese Abdominal Multimodal Medical Image Dataset

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image registration and fusion are crucial for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and providing comprehensive clinical insights. This technology addresses the limitations of single-modality imaging, which can only reflect partial characteristics of tissues or lesions, and is particularly important for diseases like tumors and COVID-19. The goal is to integrate complementary features from different modalities (e.g., CT/PET) to provide comprehensive and robust support for precise lesion detection and surgical treatment.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed Imaging Coupled Filtering (ICF) method is a unified multi-channel framework for multimodal medical image registration and fusion. It consists of three main steps: 1. Channel Decomposition: Source images from different modalities are decomposed into four feature channels: smoothing, texture, contour, and edge. This involves global blurring with a Gaussian filter, energy aggregation using a bilateral filter, and guided filtering. Multi-level differences between these images generate the ISL, ITL, ICL, and IEL channels. 2. Intra-channel Fusion: Specific strategies are applied to each channel. For smoothing channels (SLs), a visual saliency decomposition strategy is used, fusing high-pass sub-bands (1st-4th layers) with Graph-based Visual Saliency (GBVS), high-pass sub-bands (5th layer) with Pulse-Coupled Neural Networks (PCNN), and low-pass sub-bands with Phase Congruency (PC), followed by inverse NSCT reconstruction. For texture channels (TLs), an energy measurement (EM) property, image entropy (IE), and edge density (ED) are combined into a texture enhancement (TE) operator. For contour channels (CLs), Phase Congruency (PC) is employed. For edge channels (ELs), the Local Gradient Energy (LGE) operator is used. 3. Feather Coupling: The final fused image is reconstructed by combining the fused feature channels (FSL, FTL, FCL, FEL) using coupling coefficients (Î±, Î², Î³, Î´) to balance frequency components, address spectral distortion, and enhance structural and semantic information.
details.dataset_description: The study utilized two main datasets. The first is a publicly available dataset from the Harvard Medical School website, comprising 59 groups of CT/MR image pairs and 86 groups of MR/PET image pairs, all with a resolution of 256x256, used for brain images. The second is a newly registered and released multimodal abdominal medical image dataset (Ab-MI), specifically for research purposes. This dataset consists of 403 groups of abdominal images collected across four imaging modalities and five disease categories. It includes 74 groups of MR-T1/MR-T2 image pairs from three patients and 329 groups of CT/PET image pairs from two other patients. All Ab-MI images were de-identified, anonymized, and had a resolution of 256x256. A FourierNet-based registration method was used to achieve high-precision cross-modality spatial alignment for the Ab-MI dataset.

metadata.title: Impact of Patient-Driven Meal Management Errors on Type 1 Diabetes Control: A Sensitivity Analysis

details.application_detail: The paper investigates the impact of patient-driven meal management errors (carb counting error, delayed announcement, unannounced meals) on the glycemic control achieved by a "hybrid" Artificial Pancreas (AP) system for Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) patients. The goal is to quantitatively assess how these inaccuracies affect AP performance to help patients prioritize impactful factors, guide healthcare providers in training, and inform AP system design.
details.proposed_model_detail: The study performs a sensitivity analysis using the UVa/Padova T1D Simulator and the Pavia/Padova MPC AP. The Pavia/Padova MPC AP is a closed-loop control algorithm that regulates insulin infusion for T1D patients. It is based on Model Predictive Control (MPC), utilizing a quadratic cost function to minimize deviations from target glycemia and insulin reference values. The system incorporates feedforward actions based on patient-announced meal carbohydrate content. The glucose prediction model within the MPC is a linearized, averaged, and discretized version of the UVa/Padova T1D Simulator. The current state is estimated via a Kalman Filter. The sensitivity analysis employs two methods: one-at-a-time local sensitivity analysis and the Morris (Elementary Effects) method, to quantify the impact of meal announcement inaccuracies (unannouncement probability, announcement timing, carb counting error) on the Glucose Risk Index (GRI).
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes the UVa/Padova T1D Simulator (v.S2017), a realistic model of a T1D patient's metabolism. This simulator consists of 16 nonlinear differential state-update equations and approximately 35 parameters. It provides 100 different realizations of parameter sets, which were sampled from a probability distribution inferred from clinical data, effectively representing 100 "virtual patients." For each virtual patient, a 7-day simulation is conducted, with 3 meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) per day. The times of occurrence and the amount of carbohydrates (CHO) for these meals vary between subjects and are sampled from uniform distributions, matching experimental findings. The simulator also includes a mechanism for rescue carbohydrates (hypotreatments) in case of hypoglycemia.

metadata.title: ISCDFuse: Interval sampling correlation driven visual state space models for multimodal image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Multimodal Image Fusion (MMIF) to enhance image representation for real-world applications. Specifically, it addresses visible-infrared image fusion (VIF) for military surveillance and medical image fusion (MIF) for clinical diagnosis. The proposed framework also demonstrates practical value in downstream multimodal image processing tasks such as visible-infrared object detection and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail:
ISCDFuse is a novel cross-domain distance learning image fusion framework based on Visual State Space Models (VSSMs). It comprises three main components: a dual-branch feature extractor, a Cross-domain Feature Association Encoder (CFAE), a High- and Low-frequency feature Extraction (HLOE) module, and a Vmamba-based Decoder (VD).
1. CFAE: Employs an Interval Sampling Cross-Scan Module (ECS2D) to traverse two modal space domains, converting non-causal visual images into ordered patch sequences. This enhances the correlation of global features across different modalities.
2. HLOE: Consists of a Base Vmamba Encoder (BVE) and a Detail CNN Encoder (DCE). The BVE extracts low-frequency shared features using an Efficient Visual State Space (EVSS) block with ES2D scanning, incorporating a residual visual mamba structure and multi-directional skip scanning. The DCE extracts high-frequency texture details using an Invertible Neural Networks (INN) block, which includes Bottleneck Residual Blocks (BRB) to facilitate reciprocal generation and minimize information loss.
3. VD: A Vmamba-based decoder that takes the processed features from the HLOE module and sequentially processes them along the channel dimension to generate the final fused image. The model is designed to balance computational efficiency with high-quality fusion, addressing limitations of existing methods in time complexity and cross-modal global information extraction.
details.dataset_description: For the VIF task, the MSRS dataset (1083 training image pairs, 361 test pairs, image size 640x480), TNO dataset (25 test pairs), and RoadScene dataset (50 test pairs) are used. For the MIF task, medical images from the Harvard Medical website are utilized, comprising 286 pairs (150 training, 136 test) with an image size of 256x256. The test sets include 73 MRI-SPECT, 21 MRI-CT, and 42 MRI-PET image pairs. For multimodal fusion object detection, the MÂ³FD dataset (4200 pairs of dual-modal images with labels for six categories: lights, cars, buses, motorcycles, people, and trucks) is used, split into test, validation, and training sets in a 1:1:8 ratio. Additional datasets for downstream object detection include LLVIP (100 test images), VEDAI (121 images), and KAIST (200 test images). For downstream semantic segmentation, the FMB dataset (1220 training images, 280 test images) is used.

metadata.title: Latent space alignment guided non-aligned multi-view multi-label learning

details.application_detail: The proposed model addresses multi-view multi-label learning tasks, which integrate multi-view learning and multi-label learning characteristics. It finds widespread applications in practical scenarios such as medical diagnosis and recommendation systems. In image processing, it can be used for accurately annotating images by fusing diverse features (e.g., HOG, SIFT, RGB) extracted from natural landscape images.
details.proposed_model_detail: The paper proposes NAMVM2L-LSA, a latent space alignment approach for non-aligned multi-view multi-label learning. The model consists of two sub-modules. The first sub-module learns a shared latent feature space across all views using a global-local alignment strategy based on a reference view. This involves permutation matrices to adjust instance order and projection matrices to map aligned features into the shared latent feature space, capturing shared and intrinsic characteristics while avoiding traditional matching algorithms. The second sub-module appends this learned shared feature space as an additional view to the V shuffled views, forming an augmented dataset. It then learns a multi-label classifier for each view, using a permutation matrix to align multiple labels with their corresponding features. To enhance performance, the kernel trick is introduced to capture nonlinear relationships and project features to a high-dimensional space for better separability. Additionally, manifold regularization is applied to latent labels to preserve the topological structure of instances on each view.
details.dataset_description:
The experiments utilize six multi-label datasets:
1. Emotions: 593 instances, 2 views, 6 labels, with an average of 1.869 labels per instance. View dimensions are 8 and 64, pertaining to music, with features like rhythm and timbre attributes.
2. Yeast: 2417 instances, 2 views, 14 labels, with an average of 4.237 labels per instance. View dimensions are 24 and 79, a biological dataset with features such as gene expression and phylogenetic profiles.
3. Human: 3106 instances, 3 views, 14 labels, with an average of 1.185 labels per instance. View dimensions are 20, 20, and 400, a biological dataset with features including amino acids, pseudo-amino acids, and dipeptide components.
4. Plant: 978 instances, 3 views, 12 labels, with an average of 1.079 labels per instance. View dimensions are 20, 20, and 400, a biological dataset with features similar to Human.
5. Image: 2000 instances, 2 views, 5 labels, with an average of 1.236 labels per instance. Each view has 147 features.
6. Multiple features: 2000 instances, 4 views, 10 labels, with an average of 1.000 label per instance. View dimensions are 47, 64, 76, and 240, a handwritten digit dataset with features like Fourier coefficients, Karhunen-LoÃ¨ve coefficients, Zernike moments, and average pixel values.

metadata.title: LIVFusion: Luminance-optimized fusion of infrared and visible images with wavelet transformer

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on infrared and visible image fusion (IV-F) specifically under low-light conditions to enhance military surveillance and target detection by improving brightness and detail preservation.
details.proposed_model_detail: LIVFusion is a two-stage deep learning framework. The first stage is the Scene-Illumination Disentangled Network (SIDNet), which uses Retinex theory and SEBlocks to separate degraded illumination and enhance features. The second stage is the Wavelet Transformer Fusion Network (WTFNet), which uses Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for multi-scale decomposition and a Multi-head Attention Fusion Block (MAFB) for feature integration. It also introduces a contrast equilibration loss to balance global and local contrast.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on three benchmarks: LLVIP (240 pairs for training, 50 for testing), RoadScene (50 pairs for testing), and MSRS (182 pairs for testing). These datasets contain paired infrared and visible images across various lighting and environmental scenarios.

metadata.title: LMACV: A lightweight multiscale ACmixâ€“VMamba framework for efficient multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) for clinical diagnosis, combining functional (PET, SPECT) and structural (MRI, CT) data to improve diagnostic representations. The method is also evaluated on downstream tasks including brain tumor segmentation and object detection in infrared-visible scenarios.
details.proposed_model_detail: LMACV is a lightweight fusion framework that integrates grouped ACmix for local detail extraction and a Multi-Stage Visual State Space (MVSS) module, built upon VMamba, for efficient global modeling. It utilizes a two-level multiscale pyramid design to increase the receptive field and representation hierarchy while maintaining linear complexity and low parameter counts. The architecture features ABR blocks (ACmix-BatchNorm-ReLU) and an SS2D core for directional scanning and data-dependent memory dynamics.
details.dataset_description: The study uses three primary datasets: 1) Harvard Medical Image Dataset, containing pre-registered pairs of SPECT/MRI (539 pairs), PET/MRI (329 pairs), and CT/MRI (166 pairs) at 256x256 resolution. 2) BraTS 2019 dataset for brain tumor segmentation, consisting of 285 training and 49 testing instances with T2-weighted and FLAIR modalities. 3) MSRS dataset for object detection, featuring over 1,444 aligned infrared and visible image pairs recorded in real-world settings.

metadata.title: Lvvibriocin-GK effectively reduced skin ulcer syndrome of Apostichopus japonicus by eliminating surface bacteria, modulating gut microbiota, and enhancing host immune responses

details.application_detail: The study addresses Skin Ulceration Syndrome (SUS) in Apostichopus japonicus (sea cucumber) aquaculture, a major threat causing high mortality. It proposes an immersion-based treatment using a novel antimicrobial peptide (AMP) as an alternative to traditional antibiotics which face resistance issues.
details.proposed_model_detail: Lvvibriocin-GK is a novel 17-amino acid amphiphilic cationic antimicrobial peptide (GKKVWKKYYFVLRASGL) identified from the transcriptome of Litopenaeus vannamei. It was screened using machine learning and its 3D structure was predicted using AlphaFold. The peptide exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, particularly against Vibrio species. In vivo, a 7-day immersion treatment (25 Î¼g/mL) was shown to reduce ulceration, stabilize body weight, decrease intestinal inflammation, upregulate intestinal barrier proteins (Zo-1, Occludin), and modulate gut microbiota by increasing beneficial probiotics (e.g., Bacillus) and reducing opportunistic pathogens.
details.dataset_description: The study utilized 60 sea cucumbers (Apostichopus japonicus) for acclimation and infection experiments. Gut microbiota analysis was performed using 16S rRNA sequencing (V3-4 region) on samples from treatment and control groups. Bacterial strains for antimicrobial assays were sourced from the China General Microbiological Culture Collection Center (CGMCC) and other research institutes.

metadata.title: M2OCNN: Many-to-One Collaboration Neural Networks for simultaneously multi-modal medical image synthesis and fusion

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a unified framework for simultaneous cross-modal medical image synthesis (CMIS) and multi-modal medical image fusion (MMIF), specifically designed to handle scenarios with missing modalities in clinical diagnostics.
details.proposed_model_detail: M2OCNN (Many-to-One Collaboration Neural Network) is a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture consisting of three main modules: the Parallel Untangling Hybrid Network (PUHN) for feature disentanglement, the Comprehensive Feature Router (CFR) for task-specific feature translation and fusion, and the Series Omni-modal Hybrid Network (SOHN) for image reconstruction. It introduces two transformer variants, Coarsormer and ReCoarsormer, which utilize a mixed-resolution attention mechanism to prioritize low-frequency structural information and suppress high-frequency noise.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on three datasets: 1) IXI: 578 subjects with T1, T2, and PD MRI scans, using a 30/10/20 split for training, validation, and testing. 2) BRATS: Multi-contrast MRI (T1, T2, post-contrast T2, FLAIR) from 60 subjects, also using a 30/10/20 split. 3) Harvard Medical Dataset (Whole Brain Atlas): A subset of 286 MRI-CT image pairs, with 60 pairs utilized for five-fold cross-validation.

metadata.title: Machine learning to assess troglofauna occurrences in the northern part of Western Australia

details.application_detail: The study focuses on predicting the occurrence of troglofauna (subterranean air-breathing organisms) in the Pilbara region of Western Australia to support environmental impact assessments (EIA) for mining activities.
details.proposed_model_detail: The researchers developed Species Distribution Models (SDMs) using the Random Forest (RF) algorithm. The methodology includes a rigorous data filtering process to handle opportunistic sampling, variable selection to remove redundancy, and threshold optimization using Youdenâ€™s J statistic and the Closest Topleft method to address class imbalance and improve predictive accuracy across two distinct calibration areas.
details.dataset_description: The dataset was sourced from the Western Australian Biodiversity Science Institute and includes 79,503 records of subterranean fauna. After filtering for troglofauna and specific study areas (Area 1 and Area 2 in the Hamersley Range), each area was represented by 409 samples. Predictor variables include 29 environmental features categorized into temporal, climate, topographic, soil, and geological data.

metadata.title: Mamba-based hybrid network for multi-modality feature fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-modality image fusion (MMIF) is crucial for various domains including civilian applications (video surveillance), military use (infrared night vision imaging, target detection, autonomous driving), and medical image processing (diagnosis, treatment decisions). IVF combines thermal information from infrared images with texture details from visible images for higher visibility and recognizability in complex environments. MIF integrates information from different medical imaging techniques like MRI (soft tissue contrast), CT (bone details), PET (molecular-level metabolic info), and SPECT (blood flow, metabolism) to provide comprehensive data for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning, overcoming limitations of single-modality images.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed MHNet is a Mamba-CNN-based hybrid network with a two-stage training strategy. In Stage 1, separate Mamba-based and CNN-based encoders process different modality images. The Mamba encoder uses VSS Blocks and CBAM, while the CNN encoder incorporates Invertible Blocks. Features are then fused and reconstructed by a Mamba-based decoder. In Stage 2, a shared encoder (with VSS Blocks and Invertible Blocks) processes both modalities, followed by feature interaction and fusion. An Edge Enhancement Module (EEM), based on the Sobel operator, is used to emphasize edge features. VSS Blocks coordinate multi-source information and reduce loss. CBAM adaptively identifies and emphasizes important channel and spatial information. Invertible Blocks ensure lossless information transfer and reconstruct image details. The network aims to extract specific features of different modalities and shared features among modalities, achieving high-quality, information-rich fusion results.
details.dataset_description: For infrared and visible image fusion, three benchmark datasets are used: MSRS (1083 training pairs, 361 test pairs, covering varying illumination conditions like daytime, night, low-light), M3FD (250 training pairs, 47 test pairs, including city roads and highways scenes), and TNO (25 test pairs, featuring urban and rural environments). For medical image fusion, 286 image pairs from the Harvard Medical Website are used (150 training, 136 testing). This includes 21 MRI-CT pairs (CT for bones/high-density tissues, MRI for soft tissue), 42 MRI-PET pairs (PET for metabolic/functional info), and 73 MRI-SPECT pairs (SPECT for blood flow/metabolism). All images are resized to 128x128 patches, visible images converted to grayscale, and contrast-based filtering applied.

metadata.title: Medical image fusion based on deep neural network via morphologically processed residuals

details.application_detail: Medical image fusion aims to integrate complementary information from multiple imaging modalities (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT) to produce a single, highly informative fused image. This enhances intrinsic statistical properties, supports more accurate diagnosis, and facilitates effective treatment planning by overcoming the limitations of individual images, which often lack comprehensive structural and functional features.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method is a deep neural network (DNN) based framework that integrates morphologically processed residuals for medical image fusion. It consists of four main stages: DNN-based weight map generation, morphological processing of residuals, Laplacian and Gaussian pyramid decomposition, and fusion of coefficients. The DNN is trained to map source images into weight maps, overcoming limitations of traditional activity-level measurements. It uses convolutional layers and max pooling, eliminating fully connected layers for efficiency. The network converts fully connected layers into convolutional layers (8x8x512 kernel) to process images of any size and generate dense prediction maps. Image pyramids (Laplacian for source images, Gaussian for weight maps) are used for multi-scale decomposition. Residuals are derived from the difference between the weight map and its linear low-pass filtered version. These residuals undergo morphological processing (reconstruction and area opening) guided by a linear filter to emphasize high-amplitude regions, preserve structural boundaries, and reduce artifacts. A local similarity-based adaptive rule determines the fusion mode for decomposed coefficients: a weighted-average mode (using DNN-generated weights) if similarity is high, or a choose-max rule (based on absolute coefficient values) if similarity is low. An edge-preserving strategy combines linear low-pass filtering with nonlinear morphological operations. The method also includes a tunable contrast control mechanism.
details.dataset_description: The study uses three types of medical image dataset pairs: CT-MRI, MRI-SPECT, and MRI-PET. All images are sourced from The Whole Brain Atlas, a publicly available medical imaging resource. Each image has a size of 256x256 pixels. For each dataset type, 60 image pairings were used for training the neural network, and 25 image pairings were utilized for testing purposes.

metadata.title: Medical image fusion for enhanced edge adaptive Level Set
metadata.proposed_model_name: Enhanced Edge Adaptive Level Set (ABC model)
image_transform_model: Multi-dictionary Decision and Kernel Energy-based Rule
Gradient Domain Guided Filtering Random Walk

details.application_detail: Brain tumors, specifically gliomas, are serious diseases. Medical imaging modalities like CT, MRI, PET, and SPECT are used to detect lesion areas. However, single-modality imaging is often insufficient to comprehensively reveal pathological characteristics due to heterogeneity, complex tissue structures, and unclear boundaries. Multimodal medical image fusion aims to combine information from different modalities (e.g., MRI sequences with PET or SPECT) into a single, rich result image to enhance edge and contrast, reduce noise, and improve diagnostic accuracy for glioma patients.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method, named 'Medical image fusion for enhanced edge adaptive Level Set', introduces an Additive Bias Correction (ABC) model for adaptive image decomposition. It first enhances input images. Then, the ABC model decomposes the enhanced images into a base layer, a strong edge layer, and a weak edge layer. This decomposition aims to preserve important edge and structural information while reducing noise and correcting grayscale bias. For the strong edge layer, a full-direction edge intensity extraction (FDET) method is used, calculating weights based on the sum of eigenvalues of covariance matrices in different directions (horizontal, vertical, main diagonal, and secondary diagonal). For the weak edge layer, a covariance filtering method is designed, evaluating correlation between image channels using the covariance matrix to calculate fusion weights. Finally, the fused image is reconstructed by linearly adding the fused base layer (using VSM-WLS), strong edge layer, and weak edge layer.
details.dataset_description: The study uses a public dataset from Harvard Medical School (AANLIB), available at http://www.med.harvard.edu/aanlib/home.html. This database provides rich and registered multimodal medical images. The dataset includes different modality images of four patients with glioma, totaling eighty pairs of medical images. These pairs include: 10 MR-T1 and MR-Gad (256x256, Grayscale), 10 MR-T2 and MR-Gad (256x256, Grayscale), 10 MR-T2 and MR-PD (256x256, Grayscale), 20 MR-Gad and PET (256x256 and 256x256x3, Grayscale and Color), 10 MR-T2 and PET (256x256 and 256x256x3, Grayscale and Color), and 30 MR-T2 and SPECT (256x256 and 256x256x3, Grayscale and Color). The total number of pairs is 90.

metadata.title: MFS-Fusion: Mamba-integrated deep multi-modal image fusion framework with multi-scale fourier enhancement and spatial calibration

details.application_detail: Multi-modal image fusion (MMIF) significantly enhances visual quality and improves the accuracy of medical diagnoses by combining complementary information from multiple modalities. Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to highlight salient objects and retain rich texture details. Medical image fusion (MIF) integrates information from modalities like CT, MRI, PET, and SPECT to provide comprehensive anatomical and functional information for clinical diagnosis. For example, CT excels in skeletal structures, MRI in soft tissue, and PET/SPECT in metabolic-functional information. The fused images generated by MFS-Fusion also significantly enhance the performance of downstream tasks, such as object detection and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: MFS-Fusion is an innovative deep multi-modal image fusion framework with an encoder-decoder architecture. It addresses challenges like insufficient global modeling, lack of frequency domain information, and cross-scale contextual information capture. The framework consists of two core novel modules: 1) Multi-Scale Fourier Enhancement Module (MS-FEM) and 2) Cross-Scale Spatial Refinement Module (CS-SRM). The MS-FEM adaptively aligns different modal features in the spatial domain using a spatial attention mechanism, then decomposes features into sub-groups, and employs an inflated convolutional network to capture multi-scale contextual information. It maps spatial-domain features to the frequency-domain space and introduces a Frequency Multi-Head Self-Attention (FMHSA) mechanism to utilize global correlation of spectral features, enhancing detail fidelity and semantic understanding. The CS-SRM ensures precise feature alignment and edge preservation by implementing accurate spatial alignment and refinement of features at different scales, enhancing contrast ratio and edge clarity. The encoder stage uses a Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) as the backbone network for multi-scale feature representation. The model integrates Mamba-SSM within the CS-SRM for efficient long-range dependency modeling and leverages its selective mechanism to dynamically focus on or ignore input information based on the current context.
details.dataset_description: For infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) tasks, the study uses three public benchmark datasets: RoadScene, MSRS, and TNO. MSRS includes 1,083 pairs for training and 361 pairs for testing. RoadScene has 42 pairs for testing, and TNO has 37 pairs for testing. TNO dataset fuses grayscale images, while MSRS and RoadScene fuse RGB images with grayscale images. For medical image fusion (MIF) tasks, the Harvard dataset is utilized, including CT-MRI (164 training pairs, 20 testing pairs), PET-MRI (214 training pairs, 55 testing pairs), and SPECT-MRI (283 training pairs, 77 testing pairs). Additionally, a challenging subset from the LLVIP test set is used for robustness evaluation, comprising image pairs with real-world degradations like low light, motion blur, over-exposure, and atmospheric interference.

metadata.title: MMCL: Meta-mutual contrastive learning for multi-modal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper addresses multi-modal medical image fusion (MMIF) to combine anatomical and functional information for clinical diagnosis. It also evaluates the model's performance on infrared and visible image fusion tasks to demonstrate its generalization capabilities.
details.proposed_model_detail: MMCL is a meta-learning based framework that utilizes a Siamese coupled auto-encoder (MCCAE) and a feature fusion decoder (FD). The MCCAE is designed to extract both invariant and unique features from source image pairs using a mutual contrastive loss based on InfoNCE. The framework uses meta-learning to pre-train an optimal meta-representation across multiple fusion subtasks (e.g., CT&MRI, MRI&PET), which is then fine-tuned on specific tasks with limited data. The decoder incorporates Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) and a feature assistance mechanism to reconstruct high-quality fused images.
details.dataset_description: The medical experiments use the Harvard Medical School (AAN LIB) dataset, with 10 pairs for training and 30 pairs for testing across CT&MRI, MRI&MRI, and MRI&PET/SPECT modalities. For infrared-visible fusion, the model is trained on 12 pairs and tested on 60 pairs from the MSRS, NIR, and TNO datasets. All images are registered and processed at a resolution of 256x256.

metadata.title: MMIF-INet: Multimodal medical image fusion by invertible network

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a method for multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF) to integrate anatomical information from MRI with functional information from PET or SPECT. It also demonstrates the model's effectiveness in infrared and visible (IR-VIS) image fusion tasks.
details.proposed_model_detail: MMIF-INet is an invertible fusion network that directly processes multichannel color images. It utilizes an IB-DWT module, which integrates Invertible Blocks (IB) for lossless feature extraction and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for multiscale downsampling. The architecture ensures reversibility in the initial fusion stage to prevent information loss. A Multiscale Fusion Module (MSFM) is employed to adaptively aggregate features across different scales and modalities. The model is trained using a hybrid loss function that balances structure, gradient, pixel intensity, and chromaticity to maintain color fidelity and detail.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on two main datasets: 1) The Harvard Medical School dataset, which includes brain disease images (MRI, PET, SPECT) of size 256x256. Training used 40 MRI-PET and 50 MRI-SPECT pairs; testing used two sets of 50 pairs each. 2) The MSRS dataset for IR-VIS fusion, containing 1083 training pairs and 361 test pairs, with images cropped to 256x256 pixels.

metadata.title: MMIF-VAEFusion: An end-to-end multi-modal medical image fusion network using vector quantized variational auto-encoder

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a method for multi-modal medical image fusion (specifically CT-MRI, PET-MRI, and SPECT-MRI) to assist radiologists and oncologists in diagnosis by consolidating complementary anatomical and functional information into a single image.
details.proposed_model_detail: MMIF-VAEFusion is an end-to-end network based on a Vector Quantized Variational Auto-Encoder (VQ-VAE). It utilizes a dual-channel fusion rule module named ResF, which integrates Res2Net modules for multi-scale feature extraction and spatial attention mechanisms to enhance fusion performance. The network is trained in two stages: the first stage trains the VQ-VAE for feature encoding and reconstruction, and the second stage trains the ResF fusion layer while keeping the VQ-VAE weights fixed.
details.dataset_description: The study uses 5000 images from the MS-COCO dataset for the first stage of training (feature encoding/reconstruction). For the second stage (fusion rule training) and testing, it uses the Harvard Medical School registered medical image database. The test set comprises 50 pairs of CT-MRI images, 20 pairs of PET-MRI images, and 30 pairs of SPECT-MRI images.

metadata.title: MMIFprompt: Efficient modality-aware prompting for multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) for integrating complementary information from different imaging modalities (CT, MRI, PET, SPECT) to improve diagnostic accuracy and pathological understanding. The method is also evaluated on downstream medical image segmentation tasks.
details.proposed_model_detail: MMIFprompt is a prompt-based fine-tuning approach that adapts a frozen Vision Foundation Model (VFM) for medical image fusion. It features a Mixture of Expert Selection (MES) mechanism that uses content-guided prompt generation to adapt features through a modality expert dictionary. The architecture utilizes a dual-prompt design: Bidirectional Common Prompts (BCP) to extract modality-shared information and Unidirectional Modality-Specific Prompts (UMSP) to preserve modality-specific features. It updates only 8.7% of the backbone's parameters (7.1M trainable parameters).
details.dataset_description: The training set consists of 360 registered image pairs from the Harvard Medical School database (MRI-PET, MRI-SPECT, MRI-CT). Testing is conducted on the Harvard Test Set (140 pairs), the GFP Dataset (30 pairs of Green Fluorescent Protein and Phase Contrast microscopy images), and the Histological Dataset (60 pairs of Bright-Field and Second Harmonic Generation images). The BRATS2019 dataset is used for downstream tumor segmentation evaluation.

metadata.title: MMSupcon: An image fusion-based multi-modal supervised contrastive method for brain tumor diagnosis

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on the non-invasive diagnosis of brain tumors using multi-modal MRI imaging. It specifically targets the classification of pediatric posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastomas, ependymomas, gliomas, and choroid plexus tumors) and adult gliomas (high-grade vs low-grade).
details.proposed_model_detail: MMSupcon (Multi-modal Supervised Contrastive Learning) is a training paradigm designed to enhance diagnostic accuracy by integrating multi-modal medical image fusion (MMIF) and a specialized supervised contrastive loss. MMIF uses a pretrained IFCNN to generate fused samples from complementary MRI modalities, which serve as information-rich data. The proposed supervised contrastive loss then guides the model to learn feature consistency between original and fused samples of the same class, effectively capturing inter-modal relationships while preserving the unique characteristics of individual modalities.
details.dataset_description: The method is evaluated on three datasets: 1) The Tiantan Dataset, a real-world collection from Beijing Tiantan Hospital containing preoperative MRI scans of 658 pediatric patients with four types of posterior fossa tumors. 2) BraTS 2018, a public dataset with 285 patients for high-grade and low-grade glioma classification using T1w, T1ce, and FLAIR modalities. 3) BraTS 2020, a similar public dataset with 369 patients for glioma classification.

metadata.title: Modeling atmospheric impacts of amine emissions from post-combustion carbon capture systems
metadata.proposed_model_name: SCICHEM 3.4 (Second-Order Closure Integrated Puff Model with Chemistry)
base_model: Carbon Bond gas-phase photochemical mechanism (CB6r2, updated to CB7r1)
datasets: Pilot plant test data (for emission estimates)
evaluation_metrics: 98th percentile 24 h average concentration (amines, nitrosamines, nitramines, nitrosamines + nitramines, total PM2.5)
4th highest maximum daily 8 h average (MDA8) ozone

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on modeling the atmospheric impacts of amine emissions from post-combustion carbon capture systems. Specifically, it simulates the air quality impacts of amine-based CO2 capture systems applied to natural gas combined cycle (NGCC) and coal-fired power plants in the Midwest and Gulf Coast regions of the United States. The goal is to evaluate the formation and concentrations of potentially harmful products like nitrosamines, nitramines, and PM2.5, as well as ozone, under different amine solvents and wash configurations (water wash and acid wash).
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method utilizes SCICHEM 3.4, an adapted version of the Second-Order Closure Integrated Puff Model with Chemistry (SCICHEM). SCICHEM is an open-source Lagrangian photochemical puff model that incorporates detailed gas-phase and aerosol/aqueous-phase chemistry. For this study, SCICHEM 3.3 was updated to SCICHEM 3.4 by updating the Carbon Bond mechanism from CB6r2 to CB7r1 and adding specific amine chemistry and particulate amine formation mechanisms. It simulates the transport and atmospheric chemistry of emissions, including reactions of amines with hydroxyl radicals and other oxidants to form nitrosamines and nitramines, and particle formation with sulfuric acid. The model accounts for dry and wet deposition processes and uses a simplified gas-phase chemistry scheme for three amine solvents (MEA, AMP, PZ, and CESAR 1). It is designed to calculate both near-source and far-source impacts without artificial dilution.
details.dataset_description: The study uses annual simulations for 2016, covering two types of power plants (natural gas combined cycle - NGCC, and supercritical pulverized coal-fired - SCPC) across two US regions (Midwest and Gulf Coast). Meteorological files for these domains were created using the US EPA's Mesoscale Model Interface Program (MMIF) with outputs from the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for 2016. Background chemical files were generated using the background chemistry processor distributed with SCICHEM and 2016 air quality model outputs from a photochemical grid model (CAMx). Emission rates for amine solvents (MEA, PZ, CESAR 1) and other pollutants (NH3, NOx, PM2.5, etc.) were estimated based on pilot plant test results and recent developments in amine solvent management, considering water wash and acid wash configurations. Stack parameters for NGCC and SCPC scenarios were also used as input.

metadata.title: MRCE-Net: A multi-role collaborative experts deep learning network for multi-modal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-modal medical image fusion (MMIF) aims to combine images from different modalities to leverage their complementary strengths and mitigate the limitations of individual imaging techniques for clinical diagnosis and treatment. Medical imaging technologies provide various modalities (e.g., CT for high spatial resolution of bone, MRI for excellent soft-tissue contrast, PET/SPECT for metabolic activity) but each has physical limitations. MMIF is crucial for enhancing lesion detection, tumor localization, and treatment planning by integrating structural and functional information, overcoming the incompleteness of single-modality characterization and biased diagnoses.
details.proposed_model_detail: MRCE-Net is a Multi-Role Collaborative Experts Network for multi-modal medical image fusion. It employs a dual-branch encoder to extract modality-specific features, integrating a window-based Transformer for local feature extraction and a global channel-based Transformer for capturing long-range contextual dependencies. This balances local feature extraction with global context representation. A Multi-Role Collaborative Experts fusion module enables specialized experts to jointly model distinct aspects of multi-modal features, focusing on capturing modality-specific characteristics and inter-modality complementarity. This module uses a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design with a Modality-Aware Expert (MAE) for modality dependencies, a Texture Detail Expert (TDE) for high-frequency details via wavelet decomposition, and Modality-Specific Retention Experts (MSRE) for independent modality processing. The fused features are then reconstructed into the output image via a symmetric decoder with progressive upsampling. The model balances local detail and global context, leverages modality-adaptive characteristics, and emphasizes texture, structural edges, and modality-specific information.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard Medical School multi-modal image fusion benchmark was used for training and evaluation. It comprises 117 MRI-CT, 278 MRI-PET, and 333 MRI-SPECT image pairs for training; 16, 39, and 47 pairs for validation; and 33, 79, and 94 pairs for testing, respectively. Separate models were trained for each modality combination. An in-house WHU-MRI-PET dataset was also collected, including 82 patients (37 males, 45 females; mean age: 63.5  1 8.9 years) who underwent PET-CT/MRI head examinations. The dataset comprises 82 cases, with each sample consisting of paired MRI-PET volumes of size 512x512x20 and a spatial resolution of 1.56x1.56x4 mm. To avoid data leakage, the dataset was split at the subject level in a 7:1:2 ratio, with 58 cases (1169 MRI-PET pairs) for training, 8 cases (160 pairs) for validation, and 16 cases (320 pairs) for testing. All image pairs were generated by converting 3D scans into 2D slices, with PET images rendered in pseudocolor.

metadata.title: MSRD-Net: a multi-scale residual dual-stream network for Multi-Modality image fusion in CT/PET

details.application_detail: The primary application is multi-modality image fusion of CT and PET images for the early diagnosis and staging of endometrial cancer. The method aims to provide comprehensive and clinically meaningful diagnostic information by integrating high-resolution anatomical details from CT with metabolic activity information from PET. It also demonstrates generalizability to other tasks, including infrared-visible image fusion, multimodal medical image fusion (MRI-CT, MRI-PET, MRI-SPECT), and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail:
MSRD-Net is a Multi-Scale Residual Dual-Stream Fusion Network designed for CT/PET image fusion. It comprises a multi-scale feature extraction encoder and a feature integration decoder.

**Encoder**: Consists of Stem Modules (SM) and Feature Refinement Blocks (FRB).
*   **Stem Module**: Extracts shallow features using depthwise separable convolutions and residual connections, drawing inspiration from ResNeXt's grouped convolutions, ConvNeXt's large-kernel design (7x7 convolution, normalization), and ResUNet++'s residual connections. It employs a 3x3 convolution for channel dimension increase and downsampling, and a 1x1 convolution for channel-wise information fusion.
*   **Feature Refinement Block (FRB)**: Incorporates ScConv modules to integrate spatial and channel dimensions, effectively capturing fine-grained details and broader contextual representations through an alternating structure of ScConv and standard convolutions with residual connections.

**Decoder**: Utilizes Dual-Stream Fusion Blocks (DFB) for decomposition and integration.
*   **Dual-Stream Fusion Block (DFB)**: Combines the global modeling capabilities of Transformers with the local feature extraction strength of CNNs. It employs Restormer blocks (a Transformer variant) for capturing long-range dependencies with low computational overhead, and two serial residual blocks (CNN component) for local feature extraction and structural consistency. Traditional convolutions are replaced with linear layers to enhance inter-channel interaction and integrative representation.

**Loss Functions**: The fusion process is guided by an equivariant imaging loss function to enhance consistency and robustness. This includes:
*   **Sensing Loss (L1 loss)**: Used to pre-train pseudo-sensing modules (Ac and Ap, with U-Net as backbone) by mapping fused images back to their source modalities, using a state-of-the-art model's output as pseudo ground truth.
*   **Equivariant Loss**: Constrains the fusion model to produce outputs that approximate the fused image obtained in the previous iteration, ensuring balanced contribution across modalities and maintaining equivariant properties.
*   **Perceptual Loss**: Ensures that the fused result inherits sufficient information from the source images.
details.dataset_description:
*   **ECPC-IDS dataset**: A publicly available collaborative endometrial cancer dataset from Northeastern University, University of Luebeck, and China Medical University. It contains 7,159 co-registered images from 155 clinical cases. For experiments, 1,166 paired CT and PET images were selected and split into 933 training pairs and 233 testing pairs (an 8:2 ratio by patient).
*   **MSRS dataset**: A widely used visible-infrared dataset. For infrared-visible image fusion (IVF) experiments, 1,083 pairs were used for training and 361 pairs for testing. It was also used for semantic segmentation, with 361 fused images split into training and testing sets (8:2 ratio).
*   **TNO dataset**: Another widely used visible-infrared dataset. 40 pairs were used for testing in IVF experiments.
*   **Harvard Medical website datasets**: Utilized for medical image fusion generalization experiments. 810 pairs of medical images were selected, with 738 pairs for training and 72 pairs for testing (comprising 24 MRI-CT, 24 MRI-PET, and 24 MRI-SPECT images).
*   **Imbalanced subsets**: Constructed by adding Gaussian noise (intensity 0.05) to PET images while keeping CT images unchanged, simulating modality imbalance and noise corruption in clinical scenarios.

metadata.title: Multi-channel EEG-based depression recognition via micro- and macro-scale information fusion

details.application_detail: Automatic recognition of depression by combining electroencephalography (EEG) with machine learning or deep learning techniques has attracted widespread attention due to its great potential for early diagnosis and timely intervention. The paper aims to provide a reliable and interpretable auxiliary diagnosis for depression, potentially supporting early detection and monitoring of mental illnesses.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed MMIF (Multi-channel EEG-based depression recognition via micro- and macro-scale information fusion) seamlessly integrates micro- and macro-scale characteristics within a unified neural network. For macro-scale information, it exploits sample entropy, permutation entropy, and distribution entropy to characterize global complexity and randomness of EEG signals. These entropy features are deeply integrated through a high-level fusion module using a feature-wise aggregation strategy. For micro-scale information, a lightweight, compact convolutional neural network (CNN) module is devised to learn deep discriminative representations from raw EEG signals. The CNN module consists of two ConvBaReLU units and a dropout layer. The features from both scales are then concatenated and passed through a dense layer and a softmax classifier for depression classification. The model uses a dual-scale feature extraction scheme and a feature coupling strategy to enhance shallow feature representation and overall recognition performance.
details.dataset_description: MODMA: Comprises EEG recordings from 53 subjects (24 clinically diagnosed with major depressive disorder, 29 healthy people). Average age: depressed 30.88 Â± 10.37, healthy 31.45 Â± 9.15. Acquired using a 128-channel HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net system, sampled at 250 Hz, referenced to Cz. Subjects completed a five-minute eyes-closed resting-state EEG recording. PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores used for assessment. EDRA: Comprises EEG recordings from 50 subjects (26 individuals at high risk of depression, 24 low-risk controls). Average age: high-risk 21.9 Â± 1.99, low-risk 21.3 Â± 1.33. Acquired at a 500 Hz sampling rate using a 63-channel international standard cap, with FCz as online reference. PROMIS used for depression risk assessment. HUSM: Comprises EEG recordings from 64 subjects (34 patients diagnosed with severe depression, 30 healthy controls). Average age: depressed 40.3 Â± 12.9, healthy 38.3 Â± 15.6. Acquired using 19 electrodes positioned according to the international 10-20 system, with the left ear as initial reference. Sampling frequency is 256 Hz, filtered by a 50 Hz notch filter and a 0.5-70 Hz band-pass filter. General Preprocessing: EEG signals filtered between 0.5-45 Hz using a finite impulse response band-pass filter. ICA used to nullify artifacts. Resampled to 200 Hz. Z-score normalization applied. Data augmentation by dividing continuous EEG data into non-overlapping 1-s segments, discarding the first 30s.

metadata.title: Multi-modal multi-level feature representation learning for flow pattern identification of oil-water two-phase flow

details.application_detail: The paper addresses the real-time monitoring and identification of flow patterns in vertical oil-water two-phase flow, which is crucial in petroleum engineering, chemical industry, and energy sectors. Traditional methods rely on direct observation or high-speed camera imaging, which are subjective and limited in complex well environments. The proposed method aims to overcome these limitations by using indirect measurement methods based on electromagnetic signals.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method, named Multi-modal Multi-level Feature Fusion Network (MMFFN), consists of three main stages: multi-domain signal encoding, multi-modal multi-level feature fusion, and flow pattern identification. 1. Multi-domain signal encoding: One-dimensional electromagnetic signals are transformed into two-dimensional feature spaces using three distinct techniques: Motif Difference Field (MDF), Markov Transition Field (MTF), and Recurrence Plot (RP). These encodings capture structural complexity, evolutionary probability laws, and nonlinear characteristics of the signals. Wavelet threshold denoising is applied as a preprocessing step. 2. Multi-modal multi-level feature fusion model: This network is composed of five Multiscale Information Interaction (MII) stages and one Multi-level Feature Fusion and Prediction (MFFP) module. Each MII stage has four parallel branches (three for MDF, MTF, RP modalities and one shared branch) and an information interaction block. Each branch contains a basic convolution block (based on VGG-16) for initial feature extraction and a scale perception block for multiscale feature extraction. The information interaction block facilitates bidirectional propagation of information between branches, enhancing complementary advantages. The MFFP module fuses aggregated features from the second to fifth MII stages, leveraging multi-level features from coarse to fine. It uses maximum pooling layers to align spatial dimensions, 1x1 convolutions to reduce channel dimensions, and then concatenates these features. Finally, three fully-connected (FC) layers and a Softmax function are used for the final flow pattern identification.
details.dataset_description: The FPI-U dataset was constructed from dynamic experiments of oil-water two-phase flow in vertical pipes using a multiphase flow experimental platform. It contains 10784 samples of one-dimensional electromagnetic signals, each labeled with one of three flow patterns: Water-in-Oil (W/O), Transitional flow (W/O&O/W), and Oil-in-Water (O/W). Specifically, there are 1442 W/O samples, 3392 W/O&O/W samples, and 5950 O/W samples. The dataset is split into training, testing, and validation sets in a 7:2:1 ratio (7548 training, 2156 testing, 1080 validation samples). The raw electromagnetic signals were pre-processed using wavelet threshold denoising.

metadata.title: Multi-modality image fusion using fuzzy set theory and compensation dictionary learning

details.application_detail: The paper addresses multi-modality image fusion (MMIF) for infrared and visible images (IVIF) as well as medical images (MRI, PET, SPECT, CT). It aims to improve the quality of fused images for downstream tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: FDFusion is a transform domain method (TDM) that uses a novel SVB-LS edge-preserving filter for structure-background decomposition. It employs a fuzzy inference system for significant edge detection and an intuitionistic fuzzy set similarity measure for non-salient texture fusion. To address detail loss, it introduces a detail information compensation dictionary (DICD) learning strategy based on sparse representation.
details.dataset_description: Evaluation was performed on the MSRS (361 sets), RoadScene (211 sets), M3FD (420 sets), and LLVIP (200 sets) datasets for IVIF. For medical fusion, 53 pairs from the Harvard Medical website were used, covering MRI-SPECT, MRI_T1-MRI_T2, and CT-MRI_T2.

metadata.title: Multimodal image generation and fusion through content-style hybrid disentanglement

details.application_detail: The method is designed for joint multimodal image fusion and cross-modal image generation (translation). It is applicable in disaster monitoring, autonomous driving, all-weather environmental perception, remote sensing, and medical imaging.
details.proposed_model_detail: CSHDFuse (Content-Style Hybrid Decoupling Fusion) employs a triple-branch encoder architecture consisting of one shared content encoder and two modality-specific style encoders to disentangle common and unique features. It uses a hybrid-supervised training strategy: Stage I involves intra-modal self-supervised contrastive learning to separate content and style, while Stage II uses cross-modal mutual-supervised learning to optimize fusion and generation tasks simultaneously. The architecture incorporates Restormer blocks for feature extraction, a Style Transformer for cross-modal conversion, and an Invertible Neural Network (INN) for lossless style feature transformation.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on twelve datasets. For visible-infrared tasks: MSRS (1,083 training pairs), TNO, RoadScene, and M3FD (4,200 pairs for detection). For optical-SAR tasks: WHU-OPT-SAR, QXS-SAROPT (3,000 training pairs), and SEN1-2. For medical imaging: MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT. For multi-exposure and multi-focus tasks: SICE and MFI-WHU. These datasets cover diverse scenarios from natural to remote sensing and medical images with resolutions ranging from 256x256 to 1400x800 pixels.

metadata.title: Multimodal radiological AI with LSO-Net++ for lumbar spine osteoporosis detection

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on the early detection of lumbar spine osteoporosis (LSO) using multimodal radiological imaging (X-ray, CT, and MRI), specifically addressing challenges like noise in low-dose X-ray images and the need for better generalization and interpretability in clinical settings.
details.proposed_model_detail: LSO-Net++ is a multimodal deep learning architecture that incorporates a learnable Denoising Autoencoder (DAE) for noise reduction, a lightweight MobileNetV3 backbone for local feature extraction, and a Swin Transformer for global contextual modeling. It utilizes a SimCLR self-supervised module to leverage unlabeled data and improve feature generalization. The model also integrates interpretability modules using Grad-CAM++ and SHAP to provide feature-level details and enhance transparency for clinical use.
details.dataset_description: The study utilized a total of 6420 multimodal images, consisting of 2800 X-rays, 1920 CT scans, and 1700 MRIs sourced from various public repositories. The data was split into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%) sets. Labels were based on T-score thresholds: Normal (T >= -1), Osteopenia (-2.5 < T < -1), and Osteoporosis (T <= -2.5). In binary classification experiments, osteopenia cases were excluded to avoid label ambiguity.

metadata.title: Multiscale self-attention convolution and adaptive fusion for enhanced multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF) for clinical diagnosis and surgical navigation, specifically integrating functional data (SPECT, PET, GFP) with structural data (MRI, PC).
details.proposed_model_detail: MSAFusion is a hybrid network that unifies convolution and self-attention at the operator level using ACmix modules. It employs a multiscale inception-style architecture to capture features across different receptive fields and a Squeeze Fusion Calibration (SFC) block for dynamic, region-wise recalibration of modality contributions. The model is trained in an unsupervised manner using a joint structural and region-level loss function.
details.dataset_description: The primary dataset is the Harvard medical image repository containing 354 SPECT/MRI pairs (256x256 pixels), with 319 pairs augmented to 15,631 patches for training. Generalization was tested on 25 PET/MRI pairs and 18 GFP/PC pairs from mainstream databases.

metadata.title: One-stream one-stage pure transformer for infrared and visible image fusion

details.application_detail: The fusion of infrared and visible images is a core challenge in computer vision research. The objective is to extract complementary information from infrared and visible images and fuse them into a single image that contains richer information and aligns better with human visual perception. This enables high-level downstream visual tasks, including object detection, military applications, and semantic segmentation, to achieve better results on fused images.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method, OOPF, is a one-stream one-stage pure Transformer-based fusion framework that simplifies feature extraction and fusion into a unified one-stream pipeline. It consists of a One-stream Fusion Network (OFN) and a Decomposition Network (DcN). The OFN uses several Swin Transformer blocks in a U-Net architecture to extract and fuse two modality features simultaneously. Thanks to the sliding-window-based multi-head attention, the OFN can acquire local features and global dependencies and seamlessly model their contextual relationships. The DcN is a simple decomposition network that decomposes the fusion result into the source images with consistency constraints, helping to eliminate artifacts and simultaneously forcing the fused image to contain richer information. The model is trained end-to-end using a self-supervised loss function, which combines decomposition consistency loss, structural similarity loss, frequency consistency loss, and Fourier spectral consistency loss.
details.dataset_description: The model is evaluated using four distinct image fusion datasets: TNO, M3FD, MSRS, and LLVIP. The MSRS dataset, initially containing 1083 image pairs, is expanded to 10,830 pairs through cropping into 256x256 images for training, and 361 samples are used for evaluation. For semantic segmentation, MSRS includes nine pixel-level categories. The LLVIP dataset's training samples are divided into 20 256x256 patches, yielding 240,500 samples, which are filtered to 107,569 high-quality pairs. For evaluation, 3463 samples are used, featuring significantly higher resolution (1280x1024) and often acquired under low-light conditions. The TNO dataset contains 42 test samples. The M3FD dataset includes 300 samples for evaluation and consists of 4200 infrared-visible image pairs for object detection, with six object categories (people, cars, buses, motorcycles, lamps, and trucks); a 5% subset is used for validation, and the rest for training.

metadata.title: PAFusion: A general image fusion network with adversarial representation learning

details.application_detail: The method is designed for general image fusion tasks, including multi-focus image fusion (e.g., microscopy, digital imaging for all-in-focus results), multi-exposure image fusion (e.g., filmmaking, photography for HDR images), infrared-visible image fusion (e.g., unmanned vehicles for enhanced vision), and medical image fusion (e.g., combining PET/MR or SPECT/MR for accurate diagnosis). It aims to overcome the limitations of task-specific methods and the lack of labeled data for learning-based approaches by providing a generalizable unsupervised training framework.
details.proposed_model_detail: PAFusion is a perceptually adversarial fusion network designed for concise and adaptive unsupervised training across various image fusion tasks. It consists of a Generator (G) and a Discriminator (D). The Generator is a fully convolutional neural network with dense connections, capable of processing images at arbitrary scales, using five convolution layers (kernel 3x3, stride 1, padding 1), followed by ReLU activation and Batch Normalization. It takes concatenated source images (IA, IB) and produces the fused image (IG). The Discriminator is composed of an Encoding Block (EB), an Attention-based Fusion Block (AFB), and Discrimination Blocks (DBs). The EB uses pre-trained VGGNet16 to extract robust, multi-scale representations from source images and the generated fused image. The AFB incorporates a Spatial Context Attention (SCA) mechanism that learns context dependence using query, key, and value derived from representations, employing Space-Merged Downsampling (SMD) with Space-To-Depth (SPD) and 2x2 depth-wise cross convolution. SCA adapts source image representations, which are then fused element-wise based on salience. The DBs are cascaded blocks (four in total) extending the EB structure, each comprising SPD, Convolution, BN, and LeakyReLU, with the last DB using Global Average Pooling and Linear layers. The discriminator distinguishes adapted representations to update SCA and fused representations to update the generator. The generator's total loss combines an Adversarial Loss (LGadv) and a Feature Salience Loss (LGeon), which acts as a content loss, measuring multi-scale differences between fused and learned representations using recursive downsampling (softpooling).
details.dataset_description: The paper uses five datasets for evaluation: Lytro for multi-focus image fusion (11,160 training patch pairs), SICE for multi-exposure image fusion (15,775 training patch pairs from 44 selected image pairs), TNO for infrared and visible image fusion (11,790 training patch pairs from 50 image pairs), Harvard for medical image fusion (10,360 training patch pairs from 50 PET-MR pairs and 11,830 training patch pairs from 50 SPECT-MR pairs), and RoadScene for infrared and RGB visible image fusion (12,050 training patch pairs). All training patches are cropped to 64x64 pixels. For testing, each dataset uses ten pairs of source images distinct from the training data.

metadata.title: Perceptual region-driven infrared-visible co-fusion for extreme scene enhancement

details.application_detail: The paper addresses high-fidelity imaging in extreme scenarios such as rocket launches, characterized by challenging illumination conditions, haze, and uneven brightness. It also extends its application to various multi-modal fusion scenarios, including RGB-NIR, PET-MRI, and CT-MRI image pairs, demonstrating its versatility in medical and visible-infrared domains.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed Perceptual Region-driven Co-Fusion (PRCF) framework is a multi-modal complementary fusion approach designed for extreme scenarios. It integrates advanced imaging hardware (SVE camera) and algorithms through a three-stage computational workflow: multi-exposure fusion, multi-modal registration, and fusion. The framework comprises four main modules: 1) Regional Perception Model Construction, which combines local and global features (brightness deviation intensity, Weber contrast, generalized contrast feature, pixel response variance) to create a perception map. 2) Feature Adaptive Merging, which uses Harris features, an exposure transfer probability model, and adaptive weights to manage illumination variations and enhance feature robustness. 3) Multi-Exposure Fusion, which utilizes Retinex for image division, adaptive weight calculation, and hierarchy-aware pyramid fusion to reconstruct HDR images. 4) Infrared-Visible Complementary Fusion, which involves essential infrared feature extraction (using an optimization problem with L1/L2 norms and gradient regularization), SSIM-guided regional fusion weight calculation, and adaptive fusion (combining infrared features with visible images via guided filtering and brightness mapping).
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes several datasets for evaluation: 1) Rocket-1: A multispectral dataset from an SVE camera and a long-wave infrared camera, comprising 812 images (2448x2048 pixels) from a nighttime rocket launch. 2) Rocket-2: Similar to Rocket-1 but captured at different time periods, containing 560 daytime rocket launch images (1224x1024 pixels). 3) Public: A test dataset of 60 samples selected from public sources like TNO, LLVIP, and RoadScene, featuring extreme brightness and haze conditions. 4) For extended applications, datasets include VIS-NIR Scene (RGB-NIR) and Harvard (PET-MRI and CT-MRI) image pairs.

metadata.title: Pixel-level concrete crack quantification through super resolution reconstruction and multi-modality fusion
metadata.proposed_model_name: Pixel-level concrete crack quantification algorithm (SQFormer with SRFormer)

details.application_detail: Cracks pose severe threats to the integrity of concrete structures, making timely detection and accurate quantification essential for assessment and maintenance. Pixel-level crack quantification, assisted by computer vision, has immense value for explicitly assessing in-service concrete structures. Accurate quantification of cracks is crucial for structural evaluation and risk analysis, as measurements directly reflect the severity of damage and potential failure risks.
details.proposed_model_detail:
The proposed concrete crack quantification algorithm integrates super-resolution reconstruction and multi-modal feature fusion. It consists of two main stages: concrete crack detection and crack quantification. For crack detection, RGB-D image pairs are captured using a RealSense L515 camera. These are then processed by:
1.  Super-resolution reconstruction: A transformer-based SR method called SRFormer [52] reconstructs high-resolution images (4x original resolution) from RGB-D data, recovering fine crack details lost due to motion blur, compression artifacts, or low sensor quality.
2.  Multi-modality feature fusion-based segmentation network (SQFormer): This transformer-based encoder-decoder network processes the high-resolution RGB-D pairs. Its encoder comprises:
    *   Self-Query Transformer (SQTF): A cross-modal attention mechanism that dynamically selects complementary depth features based on query embeddings derived from RGB semantics, enhancing cross-modal relationships.
    *   Invertible Feature Fusion Block (IFFB): An INN-based dual-branch structure that processes RGB and depth features separately, using affine coupling layers to ensure near-lossless detail feature extraction and fusion, preserving high-frequency details.
    The decoder is a lightweight Hamburger head [53] that generates final segmentation predictions.
For crack quantification, the algorithm performs:
1.  Crack skeleton extraction: An improved Zhang-Suen algorithm [59] with discrete skeleton evolution [60] is used to extract smoother and more accurate crack skeletons from binary masks.
2.  Spatial ratio calculation: The precise camera-to-surface distance from the depth sensor and the intrinsic matrix of the RealSense L515 RGB-D camera are used to convert pixel-domain crack features into real-world measurements.
3.  Crack width and length calculation: Crack length is calculated from the skeleton pixel points, and crack width is determined using the maximum inscribed circle method [61].
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes an RGB-D dataset collected by the Intel RealSense L515 RGB-D camera. This dataset covers multi-scale cracks (0.1 mm to 9.5 mm) across various concrete structures, including road surfaces, underground parking garages, building facades, sidewalks, and bridge components. It captures diverse real-world environmental conditions such as varying illumination, plant interference, textured backgrounds, surface wear, and geometric irregularities. Depth images were aligned with RGB images using the Intel RealSense SDK. The dataset was expanded from an initial 508 RGB-D image pairs through data augmentation strategies such as random horizontal flipping, rotation, HSV contrast adjustment, blurring, and noise addition. The dataset consists of 3571 RGB-D pairs, with 2857 pairs used for training and 714 for testing. The original resolution is 1080 x 1920 pixels, with sensor FOV (RGB) of 70Â° x 43Â°(Â±3Â°) and (Depth) of 70Â° x 55Â°(Â±3Â°), and a frame rate of 30 FPS. Additionally, an SR dataset (7680 x 4320 pixels, upsampled by SRFormer by a factor of 4) and a low-resolution (LR) dataset (480 x 270 pixels, downsampled by a factor of 4) were created for evaluation.

metadata.title: Polarization-enhanced GFNet for glint-influenced water surface object segmentation

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on the segmentation of shallow water, slow, and small targets, specifically Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs), on the water surface. The primary goal is to overcome sun glint interference to enhance UUV detection and segmentation accuracy, thereby improving maritime safety and operational efficiency.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed method is GF-CDDFuse, a dual-network framework comprising the glint-free network (GFNet) and the correlation-driven feature decomposition fusion (CDDFuse) network.
