GFNet acts as a preprocessing stage, integrating polarization imaging features (DOLP, AOP, PPR) and utilizing Retinex theory at the feature level to disentangle glint-related illumination from reflectance features. GFNet consists of an encoder (four convolutional layers, LReLU), three parallel feature subnets (max-pooling, fully connected layers, LReLU, sigmoid for normalization), a fusion subnet (three convolutional layers, LReLU), and two decoders (four convolutional layers, LReLU, Tanh for the last layer). It takes PPR and AOP images as input and outputs an enhanced PPR (PPRen) image. The CDDFuse network then fuses the PPRen image with DOLP images. It employs a Restormer encoder (Res Enc) for shallow features, a dual-branch Transformer-CNN feature extractor with Lite Transformer blocks (Base Enc) for low-frequency global features and Invertible Neural Network blocks (Detail Enc) for high-frequency local information. A correlation-driven loss function is introduced to correlate low-frequency features while ensuring high-frequency features remain uncorrelated. Finally, a Restormer decoder (Res Dec) produces the fused image.
details.dataset_description: The SOED-P dataset was collected using a SALSA camera (time-division polarimeter) in an experimental seawater pool (126 x 26 mÂ², 5 m depth) in Zhoushan City. The target was an Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) (0.16 x 2 m, matte black paint). The dataset comprises 579 sets of polarization data, collected at three distinct times of day (morning, noon, afternoon) under various weather conditions (cloudy, sunny, light rain). Each dataset includes three spectral bands (490, 550, 660 nm) and three polarization states (S0, S1, S2), from which DOLP, AOP, PPR, and VPR are calculated. The images feature bright spots on the water surface caused by sunlight and raindrops. The training data (912 sets) underwent four augmentation methods: random brightness contrast, shift scale rotate, blur, and defocus. The evaluation dataset was not augmented. The total number of training and evaluation samples is approximately 1200 sets.

metadata.title: QuatFuse: Quaternion-based orthogonal representation learning for multi-modal image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Multi-modality image fusion (MMIF), specifically Infrared-Visible image fusion (IVF) for surveillance and object detection, and Medical image fusion (MIF) for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
details.proposed_model_detail: QuatFuse is a quaternion-based framework that models inter-modal relationships in a higher-dimensional representation space. It consists of three main modules: the Orthogonal Adaptive Module (OAM) which uses Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization to decouple redundant features; the Quaternion Frequency Aggregation Module (QFAM) which implements adaptive weighting of frequency domain features via 2D discrete cosine transforms; and the Quaternion Fusion Module (QFM) which maps features to quaternion space and uses Hamilton product operations to preserve high-order correlation information.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on several datasets: MSRS (1000 training pairs, 61 test pairs), RoadScene (60 validation pairs, 50 test pairs), TNO (55 test pairs), and a newly introduced private dataset called MED (Marine Environment Dataset, 56 test pairs) for IVF. For MIF, it used 130 pairs from Harvard Medical School (20 MRI-CT, 40 MRI-PET, 70 MRI-SPECT). For downstream tasks, it utilized M3FD (4200 pairs) for object detection and MSRS for semantic segmentation.

metadata.title: QWNet: A quaternion wavelet network for spatial-frequency aware multi-modal image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper addresses Multi-modal Image Fusion (MMIF), specifically focusing on Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF). The objective is to combine complementary information from different sensors to enhance object visibility and texture details for both human perception and downstream computer vision tasks like semantic segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: QWNet is a Quaternion Wavelet Network that leverages both spatial and frequency information. It utilizes a Quaternion Wavelet Enhancement Mechanism (QWEM) to decompose input modalities into high- and low-frequency components, which are then represented as quaternions to model complex inter-channel dependencies. The architecture includes a Bidirectional Adaptive Attention Module (BAAM) to disentangle and interact shared and unique features, and a Quaternion Cross-modal Fusion Module (QCFM) that uses quaternion convolution and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) to integrate features efficiently. The network follows a progressive encoder-decoder structure with only 4.27K parameters.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on three IVF datasets: MSRS (1083 training pairs, 361 test pairs), RoadScene (50 test pairs), and M3FD (used for training augmentation and 100 test pairs). For medical image fusion, 'The Harvard Whole Brain Atlas' was used, comprising 250 pairs of MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT images, with 130 pairs for training, 20 for validation, and 100 for testing.

metadata.title: Rethinking normalization strategies and convolutional kernels for multimodal image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal image fusion (MMIF) for medical image fusion (MIF) and infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF), aimed at enhancing scene information for downstream tasks like semantic segmentation and clinical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: LKC-FUNet is a UNet-based architecture that rethinks normalization and convolution kernels. It employs a hybrid normalization strategy using Instance Normalization (IN) in shallow layers to maintain sample independence and Group Normalization (GN) in deep layers to reinforce feature correlations. It integrates Large Kernel Convolutions (LKC) with kernel sizes up to 15x15 to expand the effective receptive field. Additionally, it features a Multipath Adaptive Fusion Module (MPAFM) that uses dual-path attention and bidirectional interactions to recalibrate features between the encoder and decoder.
details.dataset_description: The model is evaluated on the Harvard Medical dataset (50 pairs each for MRI-CT, MRI-PET, and MRI-SPECT), the MSRS dataset (1083 training and 361 test infrared-visible pairs), the M3FD dataset (300 infrared-visible pairs), and the TNO dataset (37 infrared-visible pairs).

metadata.title: RFSC: Multimodal medical image alignment fusion diagnostic classification network based on de discriminator image translation
datasets: Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center Chest dataset

details.application_detail: The model is designed for the diagnosis of lung nodules, specifically distinguishing between benign and malignant types, by fusing information from low-dose CT and MRI images to overcome the limitations of single-modality imaging.
details.proposed_model_detail: RFSC (Registration-Fusion-Segmentation-Classification) is an unsupervised multitask framework. It features a fine registration module that combines discriminator-free image translation (ResNet-based) and deformable registration (Swin U-net based) to align multimodal images. The system is optimized using a combination of smooth loss, LocalNCC, and frame loss. The registered images are then fused using various rules and finally classified using a ResNext-101 backbone to enhance clinical diagnostic efficacy.
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes two primary datasets: 1) The MICCAI Learn2Reg2021 Challenge dataset, which contains 122 intra-patient abdominal CT and MRI scans (3D volumes of 192x160x192) used for registration evaluation. 2) A private chest dataset from Shanghai Public Health Clinical Center consisting of CT and T2-weighted MRI scans from 69 patients, used for image fusion and lung nodule malignancy classification tasks.

metadata.title: RSDC-Net: Robust self-supervised dynamic collaboration network for infrared and visible image fusion

details.application_detail: Infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) aims to integrate complementary information from distinct sensors, yielding fused results that outperform the capabilities of either individual modality alone. It is widely applied in fields such as intelligent inspection and autonomous driving scene understanding. The method addresses the significant distribution heterogeneity between thermal radiation structures in infrared images and fine-grained color textures in visible images. Future work may explore applications in remote sensing and medical image fusion.
details.proposed_model_detail: RSDC-Net is a robust self-supervised dynamic collaboration network for infrared and visible image fusion. It adaptively and comprehensively selects complementary cues from both infrared and visible modalities. The model introduces a steady-state contrastive autoencoder (SCAE) that leverages a multi-task self-supervised strategy to enhance the robust representation of key shared cues in the mixed information flow, promoting deep cross-modal modeling of global dependencies and semantic consistency. Furthermore, a latent inter-modal focus-guided module (IMGF) integrates a bilateral transposed attention mechanism (TAM) with a dynamic selection component to refine local-level heterogeneous cue allocation under the guidance of mutual global dependencies. A gated feed-forward unit (GFU) is incorporated to filter outlier information flows across modalities. The training process is divided into two stages: Stage I separately trains the SCAE modules for visible and infrared images, and Stage II focuses on generating the fused images by adaptively adjusting shared global complementary semantics and allocating local fine-grained cues.
details.dataset_description: MSRS Dataset: Contains 1,444 pairs of high-resolution infrared and visible images, offering rich content and covering a wide range of weather and illumination conditions, making it highly diverse and practical for real-world applications. TNO Dataset: Consists of 46 infrared-visible image pairs and is widely used for image fusion, night vision enhancement, and object detection. M3FD Dataset: Comprises 4,200 infrared-visible image pairs with annotations for various targets such as pedestrians, vehicles, and motorcycles, making it particularly suitable for multimodal fusion and detection tasks in complex environments.

metadata.title: SD-Fuse: An image structure-driven model for multi-focus image fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-focus image fusion (MFIF) aims to generate a fully focused composite from multiple partially focused images, mitigating degradation in precision-critical tasks such as image segmentation and object detection. This capability is particularly important for surveillance and autonomous driving. The SD-Fuse framework is also demonstrated to be applicable to broader multimodal image fusion tasks, including medical image fusion (MIF), infrared and visible light image fusion (VIS-IR), and Pan-sharpening, by effectively learning discriminative features and handling global-local feature interactions.
details.proposed_model_detail: SD-Fuse is a structure-driven fusion framework motivated by an image structure-boundary prior, which postulates that boundaries between focused and defocused regions align with prominent structural features. The framework comprises three complementary components: 1. A Global Structure-Aware Branch that extracts essential structural cues using a flexible structure extractor (defaulting to BDCN) and captures global structural dependencies through a Transformer module (ResT). 2. A Local Focus Detection Branch that leverages a CNN architecture, specifically incorporating Multi-scale Adaptive Residual Modules (MARM) with parallel dilated convolutions, to generate initial pixel-wise decision maps based on spatial inputs. 3. A novel Structure-Guided Filter (SGF), inspired by traditional guided filtering methods, which acts as an effective interaction mechanism. SGF treats global structural features from the Transformer as a guidance map and local features from the focus detection branch as the filtered input. It incorporates an innovative structure-aware constraint and a structure-sensitive weighting rule into its optimization function, enabling precise alignment of boundaries and artifact-free decision maps by seamlessly integrating global structural information into local features. The entire model is trained end-to-end using Cross-Entropy Loss.
details.dataset_description: The model is trained using synthetic multi-focus data derived from the DUTS dataset, which contains 15,572 all-in-focus images and corresponding binary masks. Synthetic near-focused and far-focused image pairs are generated by applying regional Gaussian blurring according to random binary masks. For multimodal image fusion, the MSRS training set (1083 pairs) is used for VIS-IR, and 210 pairs from the Harvard Medical website are used for MIF training. The model is evaluated on various public datasets: for MFIF, LYTRO (20 color image pairs), MFFW (13 real-world color image pairs), TSAI (12 color image pairs), SAVIC (21 color image pairs), AYMAZ (27 synthetic image pairs), and STAND (8 gray image pairs); for VIS-IR, RoadScene (50 pairs) and TNO (25 pairs); for MIF, MRI-CT (46 pairs) and MRI-SPECT (43 pairs) from the Harvard Medical website; and for Pan-sharpening, QuickBird (QB) and WorldView-3 (WV3) datasets, following the Wald protocol.

metadata.title: Semantic-geometric dual alignment: A progressive co-optimization paradigm for misaligned multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF) aims to integrate complementary anatomical and functional information from different imaging modalities (e.g., CT, MRI, PET, SPECT) to support accurate clinical diagnosis. However, practical multimodal images are often affected by severe spatial misalignment due to non-rigid deformations, patient motion, and acquisition inconsistencies, which significantly degrade fusion quality. This misalignment leads to artifacts and detail loss in fused images, reducing diagnostic accuracy. The proposed method addresses this challenge by co-optimizing registration and fusion.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed model, DI-MSFM (Dynamic Interactive Multi-Scale Fusion Model), is a bidirectional branch dynamic progressive enhancement and multi-scale dynamic interactive deformation network for multimodal medical image fusion. It treats image registration and fusion as a coupled optimization process to overcome limitations of independent or weakly coupled approaches. The framework comprises three main components: 1. Modality Interaction Semantic-Geometric Calibration Module (MIBM): This module refines input-adaptive, multi-scale features and bridges the semantic and granularity gap between modalities using learnable global semantic anchors and a bidirectional self-attention mechanism. 2. Multi-Scale Registration and Displacement-invariant structural alignment module (MSRD): Designed to handle large-amplitude nonlinear displacements, MSRD analyzes significant, displacement-invariant feature correspondences in high-dimensional space. It implements multi-stage flow field prediction based on the Flow Refinement Strategy (FRS), leveraging CustomSwinTransformerBlock (CSB) and dynamic convolution to generate localized flow fields. 3. Dynamic Multi-step Fusion Network (DMFN): This network incrementally compensates for misalignment-induced artifacts and refines fused representations. It models the fusion process as an implicit multi-step optimization trajectory, allowing for gradual reconciliation of semantic and geometric discrepancies using residual alignment cues. The overall design establishes a semantic-geometric dual alignment to calibrate cross-modal features using global semantic anchors before explicit deformation modeling, ensuring progressive alignment with residual detail compensation.
details.dataset_description: The model was rigorously evaluated on three publicly available medical imaging datasets: 1. Harvard Medical School Dataset: Comprises 364 samples across three modality pairs, specifically designed to test model adaptability to non-rigid deformations. Preprocessing involved removing edge labels and noisy regions, applying Z-score normalization to map pixel values to [0,1], and standardizing dimensions to 256x256 via random cropping to eliminate scale inconsistencies while preserving deformation characteristics. 2. IXI Dataset: An international public brain imaging repository focusing on multi-modal MRI evaluations of healthy adults, with 600 samples at 256x256 resolution. It includes T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI pairs exhibiting submillimeter-level displacements (average 0.5 mm). Preprocessing included automated brain region extraction, affine transformation for large-scale displacements, and contrast adaptation. 3. SynthStrip Dataset: Contains 500 high-resolution MRI image samples (256x256 pixels) to evaluate performance in synthetic/denoising brain image scenarios. It includes images of three modalities: T1, T2, and FLAIR. Preprocessing involved standardized brain denoising, non-brain tissue removal using the SynthStrip algorithm, normalization to the MNI152 template, and random 256x256 pixel image patches.

metadata.title: Shuffle-reshuffle Gradient Mamba for multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) aims to integrate information from different modalities into a single image with comprehensive information and rich spatial details. MMIF is a significant branch of image fusion, particularly for medical images like computerized tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). MRI provides superior high-resolution anatomical details of soft tissues, while CT excels at visualizing dense structures like bones. PET and SPECT prioritize functional information, such as blood flow dynamics and metabolic activity, but suffer from lower spatial resolution. The fusion of these multimodal medical images enhances the reliability and robustness of clinical diagnostics, which is crucial for effective and timely treatment decisions.
details.proposed_model_detail: The Shuffle-Reshuffle Gradient Mamba (SRGM) is a novel Mamba-based framework specifically designed for Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF). It comprises three key components: the Local and Global Gradient Mamba (LGGM) module, the Shuffle-Reshuffle Scanning (SRC) strategy, and the Attention-Guided Cross Mamba (AGCM) module. The LGGM module is designed to extract modality-specific features while preserving abundant spatial details and modeling long-range dependencies. It incorporates a Gradient Attention mechanism that explicitly models spatial structures by computing horizontal and vertical gradients to generate attention maps, highlighting critical regions. The SRC strategy is integrated into LGGM to overcome the limitations of Mamba's fixed scanning mechanism, enabling unbiased local and global modeling through shuffle and reshuffle operations. The AGCM module facilitates effective cross-modal feature fusion and reduces redundancy by incorporating spatial and channel attention mechanisms. This ensures that feature fusion emphasizes critical anatomical structures and regions of interest, such as lesions, while effectively integrating complementary information.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard2 medical dataset is utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in MMIF. This dataset includes CT-MRI, PET-MRI, and SPECT-MRI image fusion tasks. For CT-MRI image fusion, 160 image pairs are used for training and 24 for testing. For PET-MRI image fusion, 245 image pairs are used for training and 24 for testing. For SPECT-MRI image fusion, 333 image pairs are used for training and 24 for testing.

metadata.title: Spatial-frequency dual-domain Kolmogorovâ€“Arnold networks for multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multimodal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) specifically for CT-MRI, PET-MRI, and SPECT-MRI tasks to integrate anatomical and functional information for clinical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: SFDKAN (Spatial-Frequency Dual-domain KAN) is a framework consisting of two main modules: Wavelet Enhanced KAN (WEKAN) and Spatial-Frequency Integration KAN (SFIKAN). WEKAN uses Hierarchical Wavelet Decomposition to split input modalities into frequency sub-bands, applying KAN for nonlinear mapping to enhance feature extraction. SFIKAN integrates spatial and frequency domain information; the Spatial KAN uses a QKV self-attention mechanism and Channel-Spatial KAN (CS-KAN) to focus on local details, while the Frequency KAN uses Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) to handle long-range dependencies and global context.
details.dataset_description: The study uses the Harvard medical dataset. For CT-MRI fusion, 160 image pairs are used for training and 24 for testing. For PET-MRI, 245 pairs are used for training and 24 for testing. For SPECT-MRI, 333 pairs are used for training and 24 for testing. All images are resized to 256x256 pixels.

metadata.title: SSEFusion: Salient semantic enhancement for multimodal medical image fusion with Mamba and dynamic spiking neural networks

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on multimodal medical image fusion (MRI-SPECT, MRI-PET, MRI-CT) to enhance clinical diagnosis by retaining salient semantic features like lesions and organ structures. It also demonstrates generality by extending to infrared-visible image fusion.
details.proposed_model_detail: SSEFusion is a framework featuring a dual-branch Mamba-SNN encoder, Feature Interaction Attention (FIA) blocks, and a decoder with Detail Enhancement (DE) blocks. The Mamba branch utilizes Visual State Space (VSS) blocks for linear-complexity global context modeling. The SNN branch uses Time-Aware Attention (TAA-SNN) and Channeled and Spatial Attention (CSA-SNN) blocks to extract fine-grained salient features via Leaky-Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons. A novel salient semantic loss based on LIF neurons is introduced to guide the extraction of key medical information.
details.dataset_description: The primary dataset is the Harvard Brain Atlas, containing 240 pairs of MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT images (size 256x256) covering healthy brains and various diseases. For extension experiments, the MSRS dataset is used, which includes 1083 training and 361 testing pairs of infrared and visible images.

metadata.title: SSPFusion: A semantic structure-preserving approach for multi-modality image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Multi-Modality Image Fusion (MMIF), specifically Infrared-Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) and Medical Image Fusion (MIF). IVIF aims to combine thermal radiation from infrared images with texture details from visible images, while MIF integrates modalities like MRI and SPECT to assist in medical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: SSPFusion is a semantic structure-preserving fusion approach that utilizes a self-supervised learning strategy. It consists of a Structural Feature Extractor (SFE) to capture prominent structural features and a multi-scale Structure-Preserving Fusion (SPF) module. The SFE uses a transformation function with a Sobel operator to generate self-supervised structural signals that guide the SPF module in merging features while maintaining semantic structure consistency. The architecture is based on a U-shape model incorporating Residual Channel Attention Blocks (RCAB).
details.dataset_description: The method was evaluated on several datasets: MSRS (1083 training pairs, 361 testing pairs), RoadScene (60 pairs for validation, 70 for testing), and M3FD (20 pairs) for IVIF. For MIF, 357 pairs of MRI and SPECT images from the Harvard medical image dataset were used, split into 257 for training, 40 for validation, and 60 for testing.

metadata.title: StrFilter: Multi-modal medical image fusion via structure-oriented adaptive filtering

details.application_detail: Multi-modal Medical Image Fusion (MMIF) for clinical diagnosis and healthcare, specifically integrating structural details from MRI/CT with functional information from PET/SPECT to assist in disease anomaly detection and image segmentation.
details.proposed_model_detail: StrFilter is a framework that leverages a structured state-space model (Mamba) to adaptively filter redundant feature information and enhance organ boundary perception. It employs the Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance to align distributional differences between feature and data spaces. The architecture includes a dual-branch encoder using a Lite transformer for low-frequency features and an Invertible Neural Network for high-frequency features, followed by a Restormer-based decoder. A self-supervised contrastive learning strategy is also used to distinguish modality-specific features from shared semantics.
details.dataset_description: The model is evaluated on the Whole Brain Atlas dataset from Harvard Medical School, containing 807 image pairs. The training set includes 333 pairs of MR-SPECT, 160 pairs of MR-CT, and 245 pairs of MR-PET. A separate test set of 23 pairs is used. Images of size 256x256 are cropped into 128x128 patches with a stride of 20 for training.

metadata.title: SwinEIF: Explicit and implicit Swin Transformer fusion for infrared and visible images

details.application_detail: The paper addresses infrared and visible image fusion to integrate thermal target information with fine texture details, enhancing scene perception for tasks such as target detection, tracking, and anomaly detection in complex environments.
details.proposed_model_detail: SwinEIF is a fusion framework that combines explicit and implicit paradigms using a two-stage training strategy. The first stage involves a unimodal feature extraction branch based on Swin Transformer's hierarchical self-attention, trained on large-scale unpaired images via self-supervision. The second stage introduces a multi-modal feature interaction branch using cross-attention and a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)-based fusion decoder, fine-tuned on aligned image pairs. The DWT decoder adaptively fuses features from different frequency bands using source image content as fusion weights.
details.dataset_description: The framework uses MS-COCO (80,000+ images) for self-supervised pre-training of the unimodal branch. The MSRS dataset (1,083 pairs) is used for training the multi-modal interaction and fusion decoder. Testing is conducted on the TNO dataset (42 pairs of military and surveillance scenarios), MSRS (20 test pairs), and the RoadScene dataset (20 test pairs of traffic scenarios).

metadata.title: Text-guided medical image fusion using unbalanced optimal transport: Semantic alignment and cross-modal interaction

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF) aims to integrate complementary information from diverse source images to yield high-quality fused outputs. Current methods predominantly focus on structural detail preservation, often overlooking crucial high-level semantic information vital for diagnostic decisions. MITFusion addresses this by leveraging text guidance to enhance semantic representation in medical images. Medical image fusion (MIF) is a core topic in computer vision, assisting physicians in more accurate diagnosis, more refined treatment planning, and more effective disease monitoring by integrating unique advantages of multimodal medical images like MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT.
details.proposed_model_detail: MITFusion is a novel text-guided fusion framework based on Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT). It first establishes a dynamic semantic mapping between diagnostic texts and image regions via UOT, adaptively weighting key features. Subsequently, it employs an Affine Fusion Module (AFM) for dynamic interaction between image and text features. Concurrently, a Cross Fusion Module (CFM), built upon UOT and a cross-attention mechanism, facilitates deep semantic alignment and information complementarity across different image modalities. A novel text loss function is introduced to optimize the fusion model, ensuring the resulting fused images exhibit both high visual quality and accurate adherence to the medical semantics conveyed by the input text. The model architecture includes an image encoder (composed of two Swin Transformer blocks), a pre-trained MedCLIP text encoder, the fusion module (AFM and CFM), and a decoder (convolutional and pooling layers).
details.dataset_description: The study utilizes a multimodal medical dataset, created by augmenting the publicly available Harvard Medical dataset with specialized text descriptions. All images were pre-aligned to ensure spatial correspondence and information consistency. This approach leverages MedCLIP's cross-modal comprehension to facilitate efficient, key-information-focused image fusion. For normal images, general descriptions highlighting their inherent advantages are provided (e.g., MRI for soft tissues, CT for dense structures). For images containing lesions, specific details about the lesion's location and characteristics are appended (e.g., 'an MRI image showcasing soft tissues...with an ovoid abnormal signal area in the right paramedian area'). Similar descriptive principles are applied to CT and functional (SPECT/PET) images. Experiments are conducted on CT-MRI, SPECT-MRI, PET-MRI, and CT-PET abdominal datasets.

metadata.title: Towards text-refereed multi-modal image fusion by cross-modality interaction

details.application_detail: Multi-Modal Image Fusion (MMIF) is a critical topic in computer vision, aiming to integrate complementary information from multiple modal images to produce information-enriched images. Key application domains include Infrared-Visible Image Fusion (IVF) for enhanced object recognition and detail richness in scenarios like autonomous driving, object detection, and semantic segmentation, and Medical Image Fusion (MIF) for revealing comprehensive information in medical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: The proposed Cross-Modality Interaction (CMI)-Fusion is a text-guided multi-modal image fusion framework. It leverages the robust capabilities of the large-scale foundation model, Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP), to achieve efficient interaction between image detail and text prompts. The framework comprises three main components: CLIP text encoders, an image encoder, and a fusion decoder. The image encoder includes a Dual Attention Feature Extraction (DAFE) module to extract fine-grained visual and semantic features, and a cross-modality Image-Text Interaction (ITI) module for dynamic interaction between image and text features. Finally, a fusion decoder produces the fused image through text prompt guidance. This model aims to integrate high-level semantic information, preserve unique characteristics of original images, and capture scene information effectively.
details.dataset_description: For the IVF task, four public datasets were used: MFNet (1083 image pairs for training, 361 image pairs for testing), FMB (280 image pairs for testing), RoadScene (25 image pairs for testing), and TNO (25 image pairs for testing). All IVF images were resized to 256x256 pixels. For the MIF task, all medical datasets were constructed from the Whole Brain Atlas database from Harvard Medical School. The training sets included 160 image pairs for CT-MRI, 245 image pairs for PET-MRI, and 333 image pairs for SPECT-MRI. For testing, 24 image pairs were selected from each medical dataset. All MIF images were resized to 256x256 pixels.

metadata.title: TQ-cGAN: A Trible-Generator Quintuple-Discriminator Conditional Generative Adversarial Network for multimodal grayscale medical image fusion
metadata.proposed_model_name: TQ-cGAN (Trible-Generator Quintuple-Discriminator Conditional Generative Adversarial Network)

details.application_detail: Multimodal medical image fusion (MMIF) is widely used in computerized clinical medical aided diagnosis. It addresses shortcomings such as blurred feature extraction edges, insufficient clarity of texture details, and incomplete modal fusion in fused images. The method aims to preserve high-density detail from CT images and soft tissue texture information from MRI images, providing comprehensive information for clinical diagnosis, computer-aided therapy, and disease prevention.
details.proposed_model_detail: TQ-cGAN is a new end-to-end unsupervised learning model for multimodal medical image fusion. It comprises three generators (G1, G2, G3) and five discriminators (Dc, Df, Da, Db, Ds) within a conditional Generative Adversarial Network framework. G1 and G2 are encoder-decoder models designed to generate preliminary fused images based on content and feature loss. Dc and Df are discriminators for adversarial training with G1, focusing on content and features. Da and Db are discriminators for adversarial training with G2, focusing on source image characteristics. G3 is a structure-based generator that takes the outputs of G1 and G2 to produce a sub-fused image. Ds is the discriminator for G3, focusing on structural loss. An enhancement network then fuses the sub-fused image with extracted depth features to generate the final fused image. Generators G1 and G3 employ a 'Y-shaped' architecture with de-convolutional layers, an encoder, and a decoder, utilizing BN+GELU activation. G2 uses a 'Fan-shaped' encoder-decoder structure with skip-connections, performing direct deconvolution. Discriminators Dc, Df, Ds use Mish activation, while Da, Db use tanh activation. The model incorporates a hybrid loss function including adversarial loss, content loss (with Total Variation norm and Hilbert Transform), structural loss (with structured sparse norm), edge loss (with Sobel operator), and pixel density loss.
details.dataset_description: The experimental data consists of 340 pairs of 256x256 pixel images obtained from Harvard Medical School (https://www.med.harvard.edu/AANLIB/home.html). The dataset includes ten types of fusion pairs: 32 pairs of CT/MRI (T1) images (Fatal stroke, Cerebral Toxoplasmosis), 52 pairs of CT/MRI (T2) images (Fatal stroke, Cerebral Toxoplasmosis, Acute stroke, Meningioma), 30 pairs of CT/MRI (GAD) images (Meningioma, Hypertensive encephalopathy), 42 pairs of CT/MRI (PD) images (Acute stroke, Multiple embolic infarctions), 25 pairs of MRI(T1)/MRI(T2) images (Normal Anatomy), 34 pairs of MRI(T1)/MRI(GAD) images (Cerebral Toxoplasmosis, Multiple sclerosis), 34 pairs of MRI(T1)/MRI(PD) images (Cerebral Toxoplasmosis, Multiple sclerosis), 29 pairs of MRI(T2)/MRI(GAD) images (Multiple sclerosis, Glioma), 41 pairs of MRI(T2)/MRI(PD) images (Alzheimer's disease, Cerebral calcification, Chronic subdural hematoma), and 21 pairs of MRI(GAD)/MRI(PD) images (Cerebral Toxoplasmosis, Meningioma, Glioma).

metadata.title: TSFI-Fusion: A dual-branch decoupled infrared and visible image fusion network based on transformer and spatial-frequency interaction

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on Infrared and Visible Image Fusion (IVIF) to generate high-quality images by combining detailed textures from visible images with target-highlighting capabilities of infrared images. It also extends its application to object detection, where it enhances detection accuracy in normal and harsh environments, and medical image fusion (MRI-PET) to improve diagnostic accuracy and preserve fine details.
details.proposed_model_detail:
TSFI-Fusion is a novel dual-branch network designed for infrared and visible image fusion, combining Transformer-based global understanding with spatial-frequency detail enhancement. Its architecture includes:
- A Shared Feature Encoder (SFE) based on Restormer blocks to extract shallow common features.
- A Basic Semantic Construction (BSC) branch utilizing CATM blocks to capture global semantic features and low-frequency components.
- A Dual-domain Detail Enhancement (DDE) branch for high-frequency detail extraction, comprising:
  - A Multi-stream Perceptual Embedding (MPE) module with Global Average Pooling (GAP), Horizontal Average Pooling (HAP), Vertical Average Pooling (VAP), and Wavelet Transform (WT) streams.
  - An Invertible Neural Network (INN) based on DenseBlocks for lossless spatial information transfer.
  - A Frequency Domain Compensation Module (FDCM) that uses 2D Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Inverse FFT (IFFT) to integrate frequency domain information.
  - A Dual Domain Interaction Module (DDIM) to improve feature correlation across spatial and frequency domains.
- A Collaborative Information Integration Module (CIIM) to effectively merge features from both branches.
- A Decoder to generate the final fused image.
The model is trained in a two-stage manner, and a focal frequency loss is introduced to guide the model in learning important frequency information.
details.dataset_description:
The following datasets were used for training and evaluation:
- MSRS [33]: Constructed based on the MFNet [59] dataset, this dataset has an image resolution of 640 Ã— 480 pixels. It contains 1083 pairs of infrared and visible images, randomly cropped into 128 Ã— 128 patches and converted to grayscale for training. The dataset includes both daytime and nighttime scenes and depicts objects such as pedestrians, bicycles, and cars. 361 image pairs were selected for testing.
- TNO [60]: This dataset encompasses diverse nighttime imaging scenarios in military and surveillance contexts. The test set from [21] contains 25 image pairs with resolutions spanning from 256 Ã— 256 to 768 Ã— 576 pixels.
- M3FD [36]: This dataset encompasses aligned image pairs captured in campus environments, tourist attractions, and road scenes. It comprises six target categories: person, car, bus, motorcycle, lamp, and truck. 300 independent scene pairs were used for testing, with resolutions up to 1024 Ã— 768 pixels. It is suitable for fusion, detection, and fusion-based detection tasks.
- MRI-PET (Harvard Medical website): 42 pairs of MRI-PET images from the Harvard Medical website (https://www.med.harvard.edu/AANLIB/home.html) were obtained and used as a test set for the medical image fusion task.

metadata.title: Tucker decomposition guided shared latent label learning for multi-view incomplete multi-label classification

details.application_detail: Multi-view incomplete multi-label classification (MVIMLL) which handles instances associated with multiple views and incomplete label sets across domains like music, biology, and image analysis.
details.proposed_model_detail: MVIML-TAR is a tensor-based model that identifies a shared latent label subspace using Tucker decomposition of an incomplete multi-label tensor. It constructs a feature affinity tensor via kernel tricks to handle varying feature dimensions across views. A multi-linear projection is learned from this affinity space to the latent label space, regularized by a novel adaptively parameterized tensorial arctan rank function to ensure a low-rank structure. Additionally, graph-based Laplacian regularization is used to preserve the local topological structure of the data.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on six benchmark datasets: Emotions (593 instances, 6 labels, 2 views, Music domain), Yeast (2417 instances, 14 labels, 2 views, Biology domain), Image (2000 instances, 5 labels, 2 views, Image domain), Plant (978 instances, 12 labels, 2/3 views, Biology domain), Human (3106 instances, 14 labels, 2/3 views, Biology domain), and Scene (2407 instances, 6 labels, 6 views, Image domain).

metadata.title: Unbiased multimodal fusion for medical image segmentation based on dual-Stream adapter

details.application_detail: The paper proposes a multimodal fusion network for medical image segmentation tasks such as brain tumor and colon cancer segmentation, and also evaluates its performance on natural scene segmentation using RGB-Thermal data.
details.proposed_model_detail: UMF-SegNet is composed of two main modules: (1) the Dual-stream Fusion Module (DFM), which uses a plug-and-play Dual-stream Adapter (DA) to align modality-specific features and a multi-scale fusion module for integration; and (2) the Dual-stream Cross-selective Transformer (DCFormer), which utilizes a Dual-stream Multimodal Cross-selective Attention (DMCA) mechanism to filter out irrelevant information at a coarse regional level and refine features through fine-grained token-level attention.
details.dataset_description: The model was evaluated on four datasets: BraTS 2021 (1470 MRI cases with T1, T1C, T2, FLAIR modalities), BraTS-TCGA-LGG (low-grade glioma MRI scans), MSD Colon Cancer (190 portal venous phase CT scans), and PST900 (894 RGB-Thermal image pairs from natural scenes).

metadata.title: Unraveling the causal associations between systemic cytokines and six inflammatory skin diseases
datasets: EArly Genetics and Lifecourse Epidemiology (EAGLE) eczema consortium
Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study

details.application_detail: The study investigates the causal relationship between 41 systemic cytokines and six common inflammatory skin diseases: alopecia areata (AA), acne, atopic dermatitis (AD), hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), psoriasis (PS), and vitiligo.
details.proposed_model_detail: The researchers employed a two-sample bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) framework to evaluate causality. Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used as instrumental variables. The primary analysis utilized the Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method, which was supplemented by sensitivity analyses including MR-Egger regression, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-PRESSO to ensure the robustness of the findings and to detect potential horizontal pleiotropy or outliers.
details.dataset_description: Genetic summary statistics for 41 cytokines were obtained from a GWAS of 8,293 Finnish individuals. Outcome data for skin diseases were sourced from multiple databases: FinnGen release 9 (AA: 682 cases; HS: 931 cases; PS: 9,267 cases; vitiligo: 260 cases), a genome-wide meta-analysis by Maris Teder Laving et al. for acne (34,422 cases), and the EAGLE eczema consortium for AD (21,399 cases).

metadata.title: Vector-quantized dual-branch fusion network for robust image fusion and anomaly suppression

details.application_detail: Robust multimodal image fusion for all-weather tasks, including agricultural image analysis, surveillance imaging, and disaster response. It specifically targets anomaly suppression in SAR images (speckle noise, side-lobes) and cloud interference in visible images.
details.proposed_model_detail: A vector-quantized dual-branch autoencoder fusion network. It features two VQ codebooks to disentangle and fix global and local features. The global branch utilizes a Transformer-based architecture with a novel Hybrid Rotary Position Embedding (HRPE) for spatial and modality awareness. The local branch employs a CNN with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM). By using discrete codebooks, the model anchors hierarchical representations, mitigating anomaly propagation and enhancing structural fidelity.
details.dataset_description: The study uses three datasets: 1) OGSOD, containing 14,665 SAR-visible image pairs from Gaofen-3 and Google Earth for terrain analysis. 2) GF-cloud, a subset of Gaofen-2/3 with simulated cloud interference to test anomaly suppression. 3) MSRS, a visible-infrared dataset with over 4,500 pairs for urban-rural landscape fusion under varying thermal conditions.

metadata.title: W-MambaFuse: A wavelet decomposition and adaptive state-space modeling approach for anatomical and functional image fusion

details.application_detail: Fusion of anatomical (MRI) and functional (PET/SPECT) medical images to improve lesion localization and metabolic activity analysis for clinical diagnosis.
details.proposed_model_detail: W-MambaFuse is a medical image fusion network that integrates wavelet decomposition with an adaptive state-space model. It employs a wavelet convolution-based encoder (WTConv) to capture multi-scale structural and textural features. The core fusion module, CNN-Mamba Gated (MCG), combines local feature extraction from CNNs with global dependency modeling from Mamba's selective state space model. A Gated Multimodal Fusion Block (GMFB) uses a learned gating mechanism to adaptively fuse features from different modalities while preserving high-frequency details.
details.dataset_description: The Harvard dataset contains 269 pairs of PET-MRI images. For experiments, 24 pairs were randomly selected for testing, and the remaining 245 pairs were used for training. PET and SPECT images are color (RGB), while MRI images are grayscale. The fusion process converts color images to the YUV space, performing fusion on the Y channel and then converting back to RGB using the original UV channels.

metadata.title: Wavelet Attention is all you need in multimodal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: The paper focuses on multimodal medical image fusion, specifically fusing PET and CT images (for lung tumors and mediastinal windows) and PET and MRI images (for brain images). The goal is to combine complementary information from different modalities to provide richer information for computer-aided diagnosis, addressing limitations of single-modal images in reflecting both spatial and metabolic information of lesions.
details.proposed_model_detail:
The proposed model is WTA-Net (Wavelet Attention Network), a dual-encoder single-decoder fusion network. It aims to effectively enhance high-frequency and low-frequency information in the frequency domain and fully interact cross-modal spatial features. The architecture includes:
1. Dual-Encoder: Two encoders process CT and PET/MRI images separately. Each encoder has three stages: Stage 1 (1x1 Convolution, Batch Normalization, Leaky ReLU for initial feature extraction), Stage 2 (two WTConv modules with 5x5 kernels, Batch Normalization, Leaky ReLU for multi-scale feature extraction), and Stage 3 (two Wavelet Attention (WA) modules for further feature extraction).
2. Wavelet Attention (WA): Designed to enhance high-frequency (edges, details) and low-frequency (lesion contours, background) information. It uses a two-dimensional Haar wavelet transform to decompose input features into four components (low-frequency, horizontal, vertical, diagonal high-frequency). Spatial-Channel Attention (combining Spatial Attention Module and Channel Attention Module) is then applied to these components for enhancement. The enhanced components are reconstructed via inverse wavelet transform and concatenated with an identity branch.
3. Cross-Modal Information Fusion Module (CMIFM): This module is used in the fusion stage. It enhances single-modal local features and extracts cross-modal global features. It employs a Transformer-based self-attention mechanism to model long-range dependencies and facilitate information flow between modalities. It computes query, key, and value features for both modalities, calculates single-modal attention weights (SMAct, SMApet) and cross-modal attention weights (CMAct, CMApet) using Softmax, and combines them. Bicubic interpolation is used for upsampling.
4. Single-Decoder: A 3x3 Convolution, Leaky ReLU, and Batch Normalization decode the fused features to output the final fused image.
The model is trained using a total loss function (Ltotal) which is a weighted sum of SSIM loss (Lssim) for structural similarity, Gradient loss (Lgrad) for preserving sharpness, and Strength loss (Lint) for maintaining intensity information.
details.dataset_description:
1. Clinical PET/CT Lung Dataset: Collected from clinical patients with lung tumors (January 2018 - June 2020) from a Top 3 hospital in Ningxia. It includes 95 patients (46 female, 49 male). Images are high quality, artifact-free, with clearly distinguishable tumor lesions. A total of 2575 sample images (cross-sectional, sagittal, coronal) were obtained. For experiments, 1000 PET and 1000 CT images were used for training, and 500 for testing. All images were converted to JPG format and uniformly resized to 356x356 pixels.
2. Whole Brain Atlas Dataset [24]: A publicly accessible dataset of 286 pairs of medical images (PET-MRI). It includes different modal images from the same and different patients, categorized into normal (2D slices) and disease-based brain images (such as stroke, tumor, degenerative diseases, and infectious diseases). For experiments, 269 pairs of PET-MRI images (randomly selected from layers 1-23 based on horizontal and coronal axes) were used for training. Data augmentation (rotating 90 and 180 degrees) expanded the training set to 806 pairs. 15 pairs were used for testing.

metadata.title: XKanFuse: A novel cross-modal fusion method based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for multi-modal medical image fusion

details.application_detail: Multi-modal medical image fusion enables the integration of complementary information from different medical imaging modalities, providing comprehensive insights for clinic applications and diagnosis. It improves the accuracy of disease diagnosis via consolidating data from various imaging perspectives. Frequently used imaging modalities include Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Positron Emission Tomography (PET), and Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT). CT captures high-density structures (e.g., bones), MRI reflects low-density tissues (e.g., cerebrospinal fluid and gray matter), and PET/SPECT provide information on the intensity of metabolic activity. Fusing these modalities provides complete anatomical and functional information, aiding healthcare professionals in making informed decisions regarding disease diagnosis and treatment planning.
details.proposed_model_detail: XKanFuse is a novel cross-modal fusion algorithm based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (Kan) for multi-modal medical image fusion. It employs an end-to-end cross-modal interaction and fusion approach via an encoder-decoder architecture consisting of feature extraction, feature interaction, and reconstruction in unsupervised learning. The model primarily consists of two core modules: Adaptive Kan Convolution (ACKan) and Cross-Kansformer (XKansformer). ACKan innovatively introduces nonlinear spline functions into feature characterization, combining an adaptive perception mechanism to facilitate local-global feature dependencies, thereby strengthening feature representation. XKansformer enables effective cross-modal exchange and capture of multi-scale attention flows through an X-shaped interaction strategy and learnable nonlinear kernels, reinforcing multi-level complementarity and integration. The feature extraction stage also incorporates a Swin Kansformer (SKan) layer, which replaces the MLP component in the Swin Transformer with the Kan layer, utilizing learnable basis functions to model more flexible nonlinear transformations.
details.dataset_description: The experimental dataset primarily originates from the publicly available neuroimaging dataset, Harvard Whole Brain Atlas. 184 pairs of CT and MRI images and 271 pairs of PET and MRI images are selected and resized as 256x256. For experiments, 160 pairs of CT-MRI and 245 pairs of PET-MRI images are training sets, and the remaining 24 pairs of CT-MRI and 26 pairs of PET-MRI images are test sets. Additionally, 24 SPECT-MRI image pairs from this dataset are used for extended study. The BrainWeb and SynthRAD2023 datasets are also utilized, comprising collections of MRI and CT-MRI image pairs, respectively, with samples randomly selected for testing.

metadata.title: Fibroblast-derived alarmin promotes oral wound healing by activating regulatory T cells that relay pro-angiogenic and anti-inflammatory responses

details.application_detail: Oral mucosal wound healing study. Investigates how PI16+ reticular fibroblasts release the alarmin protein PI16 upon injury, which activates regulatory T cells (Tregs) to accelerate wound closure by promoting angiogenesis and suppressing inflammation.
details.proposed_model_detail: No computational model proposed. This is a wet-lab biology study using mouse models (PI16-knockout and Treg-depleted mice), flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, and in vitro co-culture assays to characterize the PI16 â†’ Treg signaling axis in oral wound healing.
details.dataset_description: No public datasets. Experimental data comes from in vivo mouse oral wound models and patient tissue samples, analyzed via single-cell RNA sequencing and flow cytometry.
